definition_zh: 现代主义；现代思潮；艺术、文学与音乐中反叛旧形式、试验新形式的运动；宗教现代主义
definition_en: a movement in art, literature, music and thought that rejected inherited rules and experimented with new forms
core_image: 一间白墙展厅里，旧画框被逐一取下，画布上只剩下不肯对齐的色块与断裂的线条
scene: 二十世纪初的画廊里，评论家在一幅打碎透视的油画前停下脚步，The gallery's new wing is devoted to modernism, with canvases that abandon perspective.
sceneCN: 这里 modernism 指「十九世纪末至二十世纪中叶反叛旧形式、试验新形式的艺术运动」（第 1 个义项：美术、文学与音乐中的自觉运动）；句意为画廊新翼专门陈列现代主义作品，画布上放弃了透视法。图中可辨识物件：白墙展厅、歪斜的画框、断裂的色块、评论家的笔记本。

pos.zh: 现代主义（艺术、文学、音乐运动）；现代思潮；宗教现代主义

derivatives.zh: 现代主义者；现代主义的

senses.title: An artistic movement that broke with inherited forms
senses.titleCN: 打破旧形式的艺术运动
senses.definition: a late nineteenth and early twentieth century movement in art, literature and music that rejected established rules and experimented with new forms
senses.definitionCN: 十九世纪末至二十世纪初在美术、文学与音乐中拒绝既定规则、试验新形式的运动
senses.example: Modernism in painting abandoned perspective and told stories without a plot.
senses.exampleCN: 绘画中的现代主义放弃了透视法，也不按情节讲故事。
senses.why: The label names a deliberate break: artists treated the rules they inherited as something to dismantle, so the movement is defined by its refusal of the old rather than by one shared style.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标记的是一次有意的断裂：艺术家把继承来的规则当作要拆掉的东西，因此这场运动由「拒绝旧法」来定义，而不是由某一种统一风格来定义。

senses.title: The wider modern outlook
senses.titleCN: 更广义的现代思想倾向
senses.definition: the outlook that trusts reason, progress and the present age rather than inherited authority
senses.definitionCN: 信任理性、进步与当下时代、而非继承来的权威的思想倾向
senses.example: Modernism in philosophy placed reason above revelation.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学中的现代主义把理性置于启示之上。
senses.why: Once the label moved from studios to thought, it named not a style but a stance: the present is trusted to judge the past.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词从画室移到思想领域，它指的不再是风格，而是一种立场：让当下有权审判过去。

senses.title: Religious modernism
senses.definition: a movement that reinterpreted religious doctrine in the light of modern scholarship and science
senses.definitionCN: 依据现代学术与科学重新解释宗教教义的运动
senses.example: Catholic modernism was condemned by the church in the early twentieth century.
senses.exampleCN: 天主教现代主义在二十世纪初遭到教会谴责。
senses.why: Here the break with the past happens inside a faith: old doctrine is kept but read through modern methods, which is why the label could be both a programme and an accusation.
senses.whyCN: 这里的断裂发生在信仰内部：旧教义被保留，却要用现代方法去读，因此这个标签既可以是纲领，也可以是一项罪名。

senses.title: Modernism in architecture
senses.definition: a style of building that strips away ornament and lets function and new materials shape the form
senses.definitionCN: 去除装饰、让功能与新材料决定形体的建筑风格
senses.example: Modernism in architecture gave the library a flat roof and a glass wall.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑中的现代主义给图书馆装上了平屋顶与玻璃墙。
senses.why: The same refusal of inherited rules becomes physical: ornament is treated as a lie, and structure is left visible.
senses.whyCN: 同样是对继承规则的拒绝，这次落到实体上：装饰被视为谎言，结构则被露出来。

senses.title: Literary modernism
senses.definition: the literary practice of breaking narrative order, mixing voices and testing the limits of language
senses.definitionCN: 打破叙事顺序、混合多种声音并试探语言边界的小说与诗歌实践
senses.example: Modernism in fiction replaced the omniscient narrator with fractured inner voices.
senses.exampleCN: 小说中的现代主义用破碎的内心声音取代了全知叙述者。
senses.why: If the old novel assumed one orderly observer, modernism assumes many partial minds, so the text itself becomes fragmented.
senses.whyCN: 旧小说假定有一个整齐的观察者，现代主义则假定有许多片面的心灵，于是文本本身也碎裂开来。

senses.title: Modernism in music
senses.definition: the musical search for new scales, dissonance and rhythm after the breakdown of traditional tonality
senses.definitionCN: 传统调性瓦解后，对音阶、不协和音与节奏的新探索
senses.example: Modernism in music dissolved the key signature into pure rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐中的现代主义把调号消解成纯粹的节奏。
senses.why: Music shows the break most sharply: the shared grammar of key is abandoned, and each work must build its own rules.
senses.whyCN: 音乐把这种断裂表现得最尖锐：共同的调性语法被放弃，每部作品都得自己造一套规则。

senses.title: A period label used by critics
senses.titleCN: 评论家使用的时期标签
senses.definition: a label applied by critics and curators to the art of a particular period or group
senses.definitionCN: 评论家与策展人用来指某一时期或某一群体艺术的标签
senses.example: The curator dates the modernism of the group to the years just before the war.
senses.exampleCN: 策展人把这个团体的现代主义定在战前那几年。
senses.why: A movement needs a name before it can be taught, so modernism also works as a period label that gathers scattered works under one heading.
senses.whyCN: 一场运动要先有名字才能被讲授，因此现代主义也充当时期标签，把散落的作品收在同一个标题下。

senses.title: A preference for whatever is new
senses.titleCN: 一味求新的偏好（常含贬义）
senses.definition: a liking for new things simply because they are new, often used with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 只因事物新就喜欢它，常用于贬义
senses.example: The mayor's modernism consists of replacing every old bench with a steel one.
senses.exampleCN: 这位市长的现代主义就是把每条旧长椅都换成钢制的。
senses.why: The positive demand to break with dead rules can harden into a reflex that treats age itself as a fault, and this sense names that reflex.
senses.whyCN: 原本积极的「打破死规则」会硬化成一种条件反射，把「旧」本身当成缺点，这个义项指的就是这种反射。

intro.en: Modernism joins the Late Latin adjective modernus with the movement-naming suffix -ism. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: modernism 由晚期拉丁语形容词 modernus 与表示「主义、运动」的后缀结合而成。年代均为约数。

items.en: The adverb modo meant just now, recently. It is usually explained as a form built on modus, measure or manner, and that link is a standard account rather than a recorded certainty.
items.cn: 副词 modo 意为「刚刚、近来」。通行解释认为它由表示「尺度、方式」的 modus 变来，但这只是标准说法，并非有记录的确证。

items.en: Late Latin modernus, of the present time, was formed from that time word plus the adjective ending -nus. It contrasted the present age with the older past.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 modernus 意为「当下的、此刻的」，由这个时间词加形容词词尾 -nus 构成，用来把当下时代与更早的过去对照。

items.en: The suffix -ismus in Latin came from Greek -ismos, which named a practice, doctrine or movement. English -ism entered through French and Latin and became highly productive.
items.cn: 拉丁语后缀 -ismus 来自希腊语 -ismos，用来指某种实践、学说或运动。英语的 -ism 经法语与拉丁语进入，后来极能产。

items.en: French modernisme appeared in the nineteenth century, first in religious controversy and then in discussion of the arts.
items.cn: 法语 modernisme 在十九世纪出现，先用于宗教争论，随后进入艺术讨论。

items.en: English adopted modernism in the early twentieth century as a name for self-conscious experimental art, and critics soon extended it to architecture, music and literature.
items.cn: 英语在二十世纪初引入 modernism，用来命名自觉试验新形式的艺术，评论家很快又把它扩展到建筑、音乐与文学。

items.en: Source uncertain: reference works date the first English artistic use differently, and the religious sense was fixed only after the church condemnation, so exact first citations should be treated as doubtful.
items.cn: 来源不确定：各家参考资料对英语中艺术义的首见年代说法不一；宗教义是在教会谴责之后才固定下来的，因此确切的首见书证应视为存疑。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same modern- stock that differ in word class or reference; the second holds art movements that are often set beside modernism.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 modern- 词干、但词性或所指不同的词；第二组是常被拿来与现代主义并列讨论的艺术运动。

entries.definition: The state or experience of living in a modern age; it names a condition, while modernism names a movement that responds to that condition.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在现代时代的处境或体验；它指一种状态，而现代主义指回应这种状态的运动。

entries.definition: Belonging to the present age or to a recent style; the adjective can describe anything current, while modernism is a named movement.
entries.definitionCN: 属于当下时代或较近风格的；这个形容词可描述任何当下事物，而现代主义是有名的运动。

entries.definition: To make something modern in equipment, method or design; modernism is the cultural movement, not the act of upgrading.
entries.definitionCN: 在设备、方法或设计上使某物现代化；现代主义是文化运动，不是升级改造的动作。

entries.definition: The process of becoming industrial, urban and technically up to date; it is a social and economic process, not an artistic programme.
entries.definitionCN: 走向工业化、城市化与技术更新的过程；这是社会与经济过程，不是艺术纲领。

entries.definition: A later reaction that mixes styles, doubts grand narratives and often quotes modernism ironically.
entries.definitionCN: 后来的反拨：混合风格、怀疑宏大叙事，并常带反讽地引用现代主义。

entries.definition: The artists who lead experimental practice; modernism is the broader movement, while the avant-garde names its most forward and provocative wing.
entries.definitionCN: 引领实验性创作的艺术家群体；现代主义是更宽的运动，先锋派指它最前卫、最具挑衅性的一翼。

entries.definition: A movement that aims to show ordinary life as it is; modernism often defines itself against realism even when it keeps realistic detail.
entries.definitionCN: 力求如实呈现日常生活的运动；现代主义常靠反对写实主义来定义自己，即便仍保留写实细节。

entries.definition: Adherence to the balanced rules and models of ancient art; it is the inherited standard that modernism set out to break.
entries.definitionCN: 遵奉古代艺术均衡规则与范本的立场；它正是现代主义要打破的继承标准。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real suffix, the real word family and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: modern plus the movement suffix: the same suffix builds realism and socialism, so it names a programme rather than a single object.
normal.cn: modern 加上表示「主义、运动」的后缀：同类后缀也构成 realism（写实主义）与 socialism（社会主义），所以它命名的是一套纲领，而不是单个物件。

normal.en: The family runs modern, modernist, modernistic, modernize, modernization and modernity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 modern（现代的）、modernist（现代主义者）、modernistic（带现代主义色彩的）、modernize（使现代化）、modernization（现代化）、modernity（现代性）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: modernism in art, architectural modernism, literary modernism, religious modernism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：艺术中的现代主义、建筑现代主义、文学现代主义、宗教现代主义。

normal.en: The movement is dated by manifestos and exhibitions rather than by one invention.
normal.cn: 这场运动的年代靠宣言与展览来定，而不是靠某一项发明。

normal.en: In art history its usual opposite is classicism or realism, not simply age.
normal.cn: 在艺术史里，它通常的对立面是古典主义或写实主义，而不只是「年长」。

abstract.en: Picture a gallery where every frame has been taken down and the wall itself becomes the work.
abstract.cn: 想象一间画廊，所有画框都被取下，墙面本身成了作品。

abstract.en: Picture a stone column replaced by a glass box that carries the same weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一根石柱被一只承受同样重量的玻璃盒取代。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hands point only forward, refusing to measure the past.
abstract.cn: 想象一只指针只朝前走的钟，拒绝丈量过去。

examples.en: Modernism in poetry broke the line and let the sentence spill across the page.
examples.cn: 诗歌中的现代主义打断了诗行，让句子漫过页面。

examples.en: The exhibition traces modernism from its first manifestos to its late echoes.
examples.cn: 展览追溯现代主义从最初宣言到晚期回声的历程。

examples.en: Critics accused the architect of modernism for removing every ornament from the church.
examples.cn: 评论家指责这位建筑师把教堂的所有装饰都去掉，是十足的现代主义。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩登主义」——把「摩登」（时髦）加「主义」，就是一味求新、反叛旧形式的现代主义。

root: 由晚期拉丁语 modernus「当下的、此刻的」加表示「主义、运动」的后缀构成。modernus 通行说法追溯至 modo「刚刚、近来」，而 modo 又常被解释为由 modus「尺度、方式」变来；这两层联系属标准说法，并非有记录的确证。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one break: inherited rules are refused, and that refusal is applied to painting, thought, faith, buildings, fiction, music, period labels and finally to mere novelty.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次断裂展开：先拒绝继承来的规则，再把这次拒绝依次用于绘画、思想、信仰、建筑、小说、音乐、时期标签，最后滑向单纯的求新。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a frame taken off the wall so that the canvas can set its own rules.
core.cn: 核心意象：画框被从墙上取下，好让画布自己定规则。

branches.en: MOVEMENT AND OUTLOOK: the artistic break hardens into a general trust in reason, progress and the present.
branches.cn: 运动与思想倾向：艺术上的断裂硬化成对理性、进步与当下的普遍信任。

branches.en: FAITH RECAST: the same modern method is turned inward on religious doctrine.
branches.cn: 重释信仰：同一套现代方法被转向宗教教义内部。

branches.en: BARE STRUCTURE: ornament is refused so that function and material can speak.
branches.cn: 裸露结构：拒绝装饰，让功能与材料自己说话。

branches.en: FRAGMENTED VOICE AND SOUND: fiction splits into many minds, and music gives up the shared key.
branches.cn: 碎裂的声音与声响：小说分裂成许多心灵，音乐则放弃共同的调性。

branches.en: LABEL AND REFLEX: critics turn the break into a period name, and the name can decay into a reflex of liking only what is new.
branches.cn: 标签与反射：评论家把这次断裂变成时期名称，而这个名称又会退化为「只爱新东西」的条件反射。

intro.en: Modernism can be read from a time word, a Latin adjective ending and a movement-naming suffix.
intro.cn: modernism 可以按一个时间词、一个拉丁形容词词尾与一个表示运动的后缀逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin modus and modo supply the time sense, modernus turns it into an adjective, and the suffix from Greek -ismos turns the adjective into a named movement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modus 与 modo 提供时间含义，modernus 把它变成形容词，来自希腊语 -ismos 的后缀再把形容词变成有名目的运动。

items.example: The stem also appears in mode and modest.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干也出现在 mode（方式）与 modest（适度的）里。

items.example: The adjective entered English through French in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在十六世纪经法语进入英语。

items.structure: -ism (suffix naming a practice, doctrine or movement)
items.example: The same ending builds realism and socialism.
items.exampleCN: 同一后缀也构成 realism（写实主义）与 socialism（社会主义）。

items.meaning: an artist or thinker who works in the modern style
items.meaningCN: 以现代风格创作的艺术家或思想家
items.example: The modernist trusted the new materials of the age.
items.exampleCN: 这位现代主义者信任那个时代的新材料。

items.meaning: marked by the manner of modernism
items.example: The lobby has a modernistic glass ceiling.
items.exampleCN: 大堂有一片现代主义风格的玻璃顶。

items.meaning: to make modern in method or equipment
items.meaningCN: 在方法或设备上使现代化
items.example: The mill modernized its looms.
items.exampleCN: 磨坊把织机现代化了。

items.example: Modernization changed the harbour within a decade.
items.exampleCN: 现代化在十年内改变了这座港口。

items.example: The novel is a study of urban modernity.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说研究的是城市现代性。

items.meaning: a later movement that reacts against modernism
items.meaningCN: 后来反拨现代主义的运动
items.example: Postmodernism quotes the old styles with irony.
items.exampleCN: 后现代主义带着反讽引用旧风格。

derivatives.meaning: several varieties or periods of modernism
derivatives.meaningCN: 现代主义的多种形态或时期

definition_zh: 文化的；与文化有关的；人文的；某一群体的生活方式与习俗的；（实验室）培养的；（旧）耕作方面的
definition_en: relating to the customs, beliefs, arts and way of life of a society or group
core_image: 一块田被犁成整齐的垄沟，田边搭起戏台，粮食与歌谣从同一块土地里长出来
scene: 山村的广场上，老人把手鼓递给年轻人，舞步一代代没有断过，Folk dances at the festival express the cultural identity of the village.
sceneCN: 这里 cultural 指「与某一群体共有的生活方式、习俗与认同有关的」（第 3 个义项：族群的集体认同）；句意为节庆上的民间舞蹈表达着这个村庄的文化认同。图中可辨识物件：手鼓、舞队、石板广场、围观的老人与孩子。

pos.zh: 文化的；与文化有关的；人文的；某一群体生活方式与习俗的

derivatives.zh: 有修养的；（实验室）培养出来的

senses.title: Of a whole way of life
senses.definition: relating to the customs, beliefs and everyday practices of a society or group
senses.definitionCN: 与社会或群体的习俗、信仰及日常实践有关的
senses.example: Food is as cultural as language: both are learned at the family table.
senses.exampleCN: 饮食与语言一样属于文化：两者都在家庭的餐桌上习得。
senses.why: The adjective takes the broadest sense of culture, the whole learned design for living, and describes anything shaped by that design.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词取 culture 最宽的含义，即一整套习得的生活设计，并用来描述由这套设计塑造的任何事物。

senses.title: Of the arts and intellectual life
senses.titleCN: 属于艺术与智识生活的
senses.definition: relating to the arts, letters and intellectual activity
senses.definitionCN: 与艺术、文学及智识活动有关的
senses.example: The city's cultural calendar is full of concerts and readings.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的文化日程排满了音乐会与朗读会。
senses.why: A narrower sense of culture means the arts and learning, so a cultural event is one where works of art or ideas are presented.
senses.whyCN: culture 较窄的含义指艺术与学问，因此 cultural event 就是呈现艺术作品或思想的活动。

senses.title: Of a group's shared identity
senses.titleCN: 属于某一群体共有认同的
senses.definition: relating to the shared identity of a particular people, region or community
senses.definitionCN: 与特定民族、地区或社群共有认同有关的
senses.example: Folk dances at the festival express the cultural identity of the village.
senses.exampleCN: 节庆上的民间舞蹈表达着这个村庄的文化认同。
senses.why: When culture marks who belongs together, the adjective attaches to identity, boundary and difference rather than to art objects.
senses.whyCN: 当文化用来标记「谁和谁属于一体」，这个形容词就附着于认同、边界与差异，而不是艺术品。

senses.title: Of inherited heritage
senses.definition: relating to traditions, objects or sites passed down from earlier generations
senses.definitionCN: 与世代相传的传统、物件或场所有关的
senses.example: The trust protects the cultural heritage of the old harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托机构保护老港区的文化遗产。
senses.why: Heritage is culture viewed across time, so the adjective adds the idea of a handover from the dead to the living.
senses.whyCN: 遗产是越过时间来看的文化，因此这个形容词添上了「由逝者交给生者」的意思。

senses.title: Of policy and public institutions
senses.titleCN: 属于政策与公共机构的
senses.definition: relating to official support, regulation or administration of the arts and heritage
senses.definitionCN: 与官方对艺术和遗产的扶持、管理或规制有关的
senses.example: The ministry published a cultural policy for rural museums.
senses.exampleCN: 该部发布了面向乡村博物馆的文化政策。
senses.why: Once states fund and regulate the arts, the adjective shifts from describing life to labelling a field of administration.
senses.whyCN: 一旦国家资助并管理艺术，这个形容词就从描述生活转为给一个行政领域贴标签。

senses.title: Learned rather than inherited biologically
senses.titleCN: 后天习得而非生物遗传的
senses.definition: in anthropology, describing behaviour that is learned and transmitted socially rather than genetically
senses.definitionCN: 人类学中指通过社会学习传递、而非基因遗传的行为
senses.example: Tool use in this species is cultural, taught by mothers to their young.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种使用工具的行为属于文化行为，由母亲教给幼崽。
senses.why: The adjective draws the line between nature and nurture: what is passed by teaching, not by genes, is called cultural.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词划出天性与教养的界线：靠教导而非基因传递的东西，就叫文化的。

senses.title: Of laboratory culture
senses.definition: in biology, relating to the growth of cells or microorganisms in a prepared medium
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中指在配制好的培养基中培养细胞或微生物的
senses.example: The team compared cultural growth rates across three samples.
senses.exampleCN: 团队比较了三份样本的培养生长速度。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the root is tending and growing, so the adjective still describes organisms raised under controlled conditions.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根最古老的意思就是照料与栽种，因此这个形容词仍可描述在受控条件下培育的生物。

senses.title: Of tillage (archaic and technical)
senses.titleCN: 耕作方面的（古旧或专业用法）
senses.definition: in older agricultural writing, relating to the cultivation of land
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的农业文献中，指与土地耕作有关的
senses.example: The manual lists cultural operations such as ploughing and weeding.
senses.exampleCN: 这本手册列出了犁地、除草等耕作作业。
senses.why: The word began with the field, not the concert hall: cultivation of soil is the literal source that the other senses grew from.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初属于田地，而不是音乐厅：对土壤的耕作才是其他义项由之生长的字面源头。

intro.en: Cultural is the adjective of culture, which comes from Latin cultura, tilling and care, built on colere, to till, dwell or worship. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cultural 是 culture 的形容词，后者来自拉丁语 cultura「耕作、照料」，由 colere「耕种、居住、敬拜」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Colere meant to till the soil, to dwell in a place, and to worship. Its deeper pre-Latin origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: colere 意为耕种土地、居住于某地以及敬拜。它在拉丁语之前的更深来源不确定。

items.en: Cultura named the act of tilling and, by extension, care and training. The agricultural and the educational senses grew from the same image of tending something so that it improves.
items.cn: cultura 指耕作这一动作，并引申为照料与培养。农业义与教育义都从同一个意象长出来：照料某物，使它变得更好。

items.en: The adjective ending -alis meant of or belonging to, and it regularly formed adjectives from nouns, as in naturalis from natura.
items.cn: 形容词词尾 -alis 意为「属于……的」，常由名词构成形容词，如 naturalis 来自 natura。

items.en: French formed culturel from culture, and English borrowed the pattern in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 法语由 culture 构成 culturel，英语在十九世纪借用了这一构词方式。

items.en: English cultural first described the cultivation of plants and later extended to the arts and to the shared life of a people.
items.cn: 英语 cultural 起初描述植物的栽培，后来扩展到艺术以及一个民族共有的生活。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English citation for the arts sense is dated differently in different reference works, and the pre-Latin origin of colere remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：艺术义在英语中的最早书证各家说法不一；colere 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds forms of the same root that differ in word class; the second holds adjectives that also describe people or societies.
note.cn: 第一组是同根而词性不同的形式；第二组是同样可描述人或社会的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun names the whole way of life or the arts; cultural is the adjective that describes something as belonging to it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指整套生活方式或艺术；cultural 是形容词，描述某物属于它。

entries.definition: Describing a person who is refined and well educated; cultural describes events, identity or policy, not personal polish.
entries.definitionCN: 形容人有修养、受过良好教育；cultural 描述活动、认同或政策，不指个人修养。

entries.definition: To prepare land, grow plants, or develop a quality; it keeps the literal action that cultural only refers to.
entries.definitionCN: 耕地、种植或培养某种品质；它保留着 cultural 只是指涉的字面动作。

entries.definition: The practice of farming, literally field cultivation; it shares the cultura root but adds the land word.
entries.definitionCN: 农业，字面即「田地耕作」；它共享 cultura 词根，但加了表示田地的词。

entries.definition: Relating to society and its organization; cultural stresses shared meaning and custom, while social stresses relations among people.
entries.definitionCN: 与社会及其组织有关；cultural 强调共有的意义与习俗，social 强调人与人之间的关系。

entries.definition: Relating to a people with shared ancestry and identity; narrower than cultural, which also covers arts and policy.
entries.definitionCN: 与共享血统与认同的民族有关；比 cultural 窄，后者还包括艺术与政策。

entries.definition: Relating to art or to the skill of an artist; only one narrow sense of cultural overlaps with it.
entries.definitionCN: 与艺术或艺术家的技艺有关；只与 cultural 的一个窄义重叠。

entries.definition: Showing cultivation of manners and taste; it evaluates a person, whereas cultural simply classifies something.
entries.definitionCN: 举止与品味显出修养；它评价一个人，而 cultural 只是给事物归类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real suffix, the real root family and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀、真实的同根词族，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: culture plus the adjective suffix -al: the same ending turns nation into national and nature into natural.
normal.cn: culture 加形容词后缀 -al：同一词尾也把 nation（民族）变成 national（民族的）、把 nature（自然）变成 natural（自然的）。

normal.en: The family runs culture, cultured, cultural, culturally, cultivate and agriculture.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 culture（文化）、cultured（有修养的）、cultural（文化的）、culturally（文化上）、cultivate（耕作、培养）、agriculture（农业）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: cultural identity, cultural heritage, cultural policy, cultural studies.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：文化认同、文化遗产、文化政策、文化研究。

normal.en: The root began in the soil: tilling, tending and worship all belonged to one verb before the word moved to the mind.
normal.cn: 这个词根起于泥土：耕种、照料与敬拜原本都属于同一个动词，后来才移到心灵领域。

normal.en: Useful contrast: a cultured person has polish, while a cultural event belongs to shared life.
normal.cn: 有用的对照：a cultured person（有修养的人）指个人品味，而 a cultural event（文化活动）属于共有生活。

abstract.en: Picture a furrow and a theatre stage cut into the same field.
abstract.cn: 想象同一块田里既开出垄沟，也搭起戏台。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe card handed from a grandmother to a child, changing slightly at each handover.
abstract.cn: 想象一张菜谱卡从祖母传到孩子，每传一次都略有改动。

abstract.en: Picture a laboratory dish and a village square both described with the same word for tending.
abstract.cn: 想象一只培养皿与一个村广场都用同一个表示「照料」的词来描述。

examples.en: Language is the most portable part of a cultural inheritance.
examples.cn: 语言是文化传承中最便于携带的部分。

examples.en: The museum runs cultural programmes for school classes.
examples.cn: 博物馆为学校班级开设文化项目。

examples.en: Researchers treat tool-making as a cultural skill, not an instinct.
examples.cn: 研究者把制造工具视为一种文化技能，而非本能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「靠它扯」——一群人靠共同的习俗、歌谣与规矩把彼此扯在一起，这就是文化的。

root: 拉丁语 cultura「耕作、照料」加形容词词尾 -alis 构成。cultura 来自 colere「耕种、居住、敬拜」，colere 在拉丁语之前的更深来源不确定。英语 cultural 经法语构词方式进入，最初指耕作，后扩展到艺术与群体生活。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of tending: soil is cultivated, then a way of life, then the arts, then identity, heritage, policy, learned behaviour, lab cultures and finally the old field sense itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「照料」动作展开：先耕作土壤，再照料生活方式、艺术、认同、遗产、政策、习得行为与实验室培养，最后回到古老的田地义本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ploughed field and a stage on the same ground, both tended by the same hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一片地上既有犁过的田，也有搭起的戏台，都由同一双手照料。

branches.en: LEARNED LIFE: a whole way of life is taught rather than inherited, which is why anthropology calls it cultural behaviour.
branches.cn: 习得的生活：整套生活方式靠教导而非遗传，因此人类学称之为文化行为。

branches.en: ARTS AND LETTERS: the narrow sense of culture as works of art and ideas.
branches.cn: 艺术与文学：culture 作为艺术作品与思想产品的窄义。

branches.en: IDENTITY AND HANDOVER: shared culture marks who belongs, and heritage marks what is passed down.
branches.cn: 认同与交接：共有文化标记谁属于这里，遗产则标记什么被传下来。

branches.en: POLICY: the state turns culture into a field to be funded and regulated.
branches.cn: 政策：国家把文化变成一个需要资助与管理的领域。

branches.en: TENDING ORGANISMS AND LAND: lab cultures and old tillage both keep the literal sense of caring for growth.
branches.cn: 照料生物与土地：实验室培养与古老耕作都保留了「照料生长」的字面义。

intro.en: Cultural is a Latin noun stem plus an adjective ending, and that stem also builds the noun, the verb and the farming word.
intro.cn: cultural 是拉丁名词词干加形容词词尾构成，这个词干还构成名词、动词与农业词。

latinIntro.en: Latin colere gives cultura, the noun for tilling and care; -alis turns cultura into an adjective, and English -al continues the pattern.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 colere 给出 cultura，即表示耕作与照料的名词；-alis 把 cultura 变成形容词，英语的 -al 延续了这一模式。

items.structure: colere (Latin verb, to till, dwell, worship)
items.example: The stem also appears in cultivate and colony.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干也出现在 cultivate（耕作、培养）与 colony（聚居地）里。

items.example: The noun passed through French into English as culture.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词经法语进入英语，成为 culture。

items.structure: -alis (Latin adjective ending, of or belonging to)
items.example: The ending also builds natural and national.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾也构成 natural（自然的）与 national（民族的）。

items.meaning: a way of life; the arts; the growth of organisms
items.meaningCN: 生活方式；艺术；生物的培育
items.example: The word covers both a people and a dish of cells.
items.exampleCN: 这个词既指一个民族，也指一盘细胞。

items.example: The festival is a cultural event.
items.exampleCN: 这个节庆是一项文化活动。

items.example: The two towns are culturally close.
items.exampleCN: 这两座镇在文化上很接近。

items.meaningCN: 有修养的；在培养基中培养的
items.example: The cultured pearls are grown on a farm.
items.exampleCN: 这些养殖珍珠是在养殖场里培育的。

items.meaning: to prepare land or develop a quality
items.example: Farmers cultivate the terraces by hand.
items.exampleCN: 农民手工耕作这些梯田。

items.example: Agriculture shaped the valley for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 农业塑造了这座山谷数百年。

items.example: The press called the commune countercultural.
items.exampleCN: 媒体称这个公社是反主流文化的。

latinEntries.structure: colere, colui, cultum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
latinEntries.meaning: to till, cultivate; to dwell; to worship

definition_zh: 在文化方面；从文化角度；按某一群体的文化习惯；通过文化方式
definition_en: in relation to culture, or in a way that belongs to a particular culture
core_image: 两座隔着山脊的村庄各唱各的调子，旋律却在同一个拍点上合拢
scene: 两个村子隔着一道山脊，赶集时却唱着几乎相同的调子，The two neighbours are culturally close although their languages differ.
sceneCN: 这里 culturally 指「在文化层面上、从文化角度衡量」（第 1 个义项：就文化整体而言）；句意为这两个邻村虽然语言不同，文化上却很接近。图中可辨识物件：山脊、两村的路、集市摊位、相似的鼓点。

pos.zh: 在文化方面；从文化角度；按某一文化习惯地

derivatives.zh: 跨文化地；在不同文化之间

senses.title: In cultural terms overall
senses.definition: in relation to culture as a whole way of life
senses.definitionCN: 就作为整套生活方式的文化而言
senses.example: The two neighbours are culturally close although their languages differ.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个邻村虽然语言不同，文化上却很接近。
senses.why: The adverb turns the adjective into a measuring rod: it says on which axis two things are being compared, and that axis is culture.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把形容词变成一把量尺：它说明两件事物正沿哪条轴比较，而这条轴就是文化。

senses.title: As determined by culture
senses.definition: in a way that is shaped or caused by cultural beliefs and practices
senses.definitionCN: 以受文化信念与实践塑造或造成的方式
senses.example: What counts as polite is culturally determined, not natural.
senses.exampleCN: 什么算有礼貌是由文化决定的，而非天生如此。
senses.why: Here the adverb marks cause: the behaviour is not chosen freely but pressed into shape by the surrounding culture.
senses.whyCN: 这里的副词标记原因：这种行为并非自由选择，而是被周遭文化压成这个形状。

senses.title: In a way that fits a group's norms
senses.titleCN: 以符合某群体规范的方式
senses.definition: in a manner that is acceptable or suitable within a particular culture
senses.definitionCN: 以在某一文化中被接受或合适的方式
senses.example: The health workers were trained to give culturally appropriate advice.
senses.exampleCN: 这些卫生工作者受过训练，能给出符合当地文化习惯的建议。
senses.why: The same act can be respectful in one place and rude in another, so the adverb adds the test of local fitness.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作在此处是尊重，在彼处却可能失礼，因此这个副词加上了「在当地是否合宜」的检验。

senses.title: By transmission through culture
senses.definition: by learning and social transmission rather than by genes
senses.definitionCN: 通过学习与社会传递，而非通过基因
senses.example: Song patterns are culturally transmitted from one generation to the next.
senses.exampleCN: 歌谣的样式是一代代通过文化传递的。
senses.why: The adverb can name the channel as well as the axis: what travels through teaching, imitation and memory travels culturally.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词既可指比较的轴，也可指传递的渠道：经由教导、模仿与记忆流传的东西，就是通过文化流传。

senses.title: In artistic and intellectual richness
senses.titleCN: 在艺术与智识丰富度方面
senses.definition: in terms of the arts, learning and intellectual life
senses.definitionCN: 就艺术、学问与智识生活而言
senses.example: The port is culturally rich, with theatres, presses and old libraries.
senses.exampleCN: 这座港口文化底蕴丰富，有剧院、出版社与古老图书馆。
senses.why: This narrows the axis from the whole way of life to its artistic products, the sense of culture as works and ideas.
senses.whyCN: 这把比较的轴从整套生活方式收窄到它的艺术产品，即 culture 作为作品与思想的窄义。

senses.title: With awareness of cultural difference
senses.definition: in a way that shows awareness of and respect for different cultural backgrounds
senses.definitionCN: 以表现出对不同文化背景的认识与尊重的方式
senses.example: The novel is culturally sensitive in its portraits of migrant families.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说在刻画移居家庭时对文化差异很敏感。
senses.why: The adverb here modifies the manner of an act: not just what is done, but how carefully the doer watches for cultural difference.
senses.whyCN: 这里的副词修饰做事的方式：不只是做了什么，还包括做事者多留意文化差异。

senses.title: Limited or bound by culture
senses.definition: in a way that is confined by the assumptions of one culture
senses.definitionCN: 以一种被某一文化的预设所局限的方式
senses.example: The early theory was culturally bound and ignored non-Western family forms.
senses.exampleCN: 早期理论受文化局限，忽视了非西方的家庭形态。
senses.why: The same axis can become a cage: what is culturally shaped may also be culturally limited, unable to see past its own assumptions.
senses.whyCN: 同一条轴也可能变成笼子：受文化塑造的东西，也可能受文化限制，看不见自身预设之外的事物。

senses.title: From a cultural viewpoint (discourse marker)
senses.titleCN: 从文化角度来说（话语标记）
senses.definition: used to introduce a judgement made from the standpoint of culture
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出从文化立场作出的判断
senses.example: Culturally speaking, the change matters more than the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 从文化角度来说，这一变化比那条新路更重要。
senses.why: Spoken English turns the adverb into a frame: it announces the angle from which the next claim should be heard.
senses.whyCN: 口语把这个副词变成框架：它宣告接下来那句话应从哪个角度去听。

intro.en: Culturally is the adverb of cultural, which is culture plus the Latin-derived adjective ending -al, with the English adverb ending -ly added on top. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: culturally 是 cultural 的副词，而 cultural 是 culture 加源自拉丁语的形容词词尾 -al，再叠上英语副词词尾 -ly。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin cultura meant tilling and care, from colere, to till or worship; the noun reached English through French as culture.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cultura 意为耕作与照料，来自 colere「耕种、敬拜」；这个名词经法语进入英语，成为 culture。

items.en: The adjective ending -alis, of or belonging to, produced culturalis in later Latin and shaped English cultural.
items.cn: 形容词词尾 -alis 意为「属于……的」，在较晚的拉丁语中构成 culturalis，并塑造了英语 cultural。

items.en: Old English formed adverbs with -lice, originally a form of lic, body or form; the ending became Middle English -li and modern -ly.
items.cn: 古英语用 -lice 构成副词，它原本是 lic（身体、形体）的一种形式；这个词尾后来变成中古英语 -li 与现代英语 -ly。

items.en: English cultural plus -ly gave culturally, first in the sense of cultivation and later in the sense of shared life and the arts.
items.cn: 英语 cultural 加 -ly 得到 culturally，先指耕作，后指共有生活与艺术。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adverb spread through anthropology, education and policy, where culturally appropriate and culturally sensitive became fixed phrases.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个副词经人类学、教育与政策领域扩散，culturally appropriate（文化上合宜）与 culturally sensitive（对文化差异敏感）成了固定搭配。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of the adverb in the arts sense is not securely dated, and the pre-Latin origin of colere remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个副词的艺术义在英语中的最早使用没有确切年代；colere 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds forms of the same root that are easily swapped; the second holds adverbs that also frame a comparison but along another axis.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、极易误换的形式；第二组是同样引出比较、但换了比较轴的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing something as belonging to culture; culturally is the adverb that says in what respect.
entries.definitionCN: 描述某物属于文化的形容词；culturally 是说明「在哪个方面」的副词。

entries.definition: The noun for a way of life or the arts; it cannot stand where the adverb stands.
entries.definitionCN: 表示生活方式或艺术的名词；不能占据副词的位置。

entries.definition: An adjective for a refined person or for organisms grown in a medium; it evaluates a person, while culturally frames a comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 形容有修养的人或培养基中培育的生物；它评价人，而 culturally 引出比较。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to till land or develop a quality; the adverb never carries this action.
entries.definitionCN: 表示耕地或培养品质的动词；这个副词从不承担这一动作。

entries.definition: In terms of society and relations among people; culturally points to shared meanings and customs instead.
entries.definitionCN: 就社会与人与人之间的关系而言；culturally 则指向共有的意义与习俗。

entries.definition: In terms of ethnic origin or group membership; narrower than culturally, which also covers arts and policy.
entries.definitionCN: 就族裔来源或群体归属而言；比 culturally 窄，后者还包括艺术与政策。

entries.definition: In terms of art or artistic skill; it matches only the arts sense of culturally.
entries.definitionCN: 就艺术或艺术技巧而言；只与 culturally 的艺术义重合。

entries.definition: In the manner handed down over time; it stresses age and continuity, while culturally stresses shared meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 以随时间传下的方式；它强调年代与延续，而 culturally 强调共有意义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real adverb ending, the real family and the fixed phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的副词词尾、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的固定搭配。

normal.en: cultural plus the adverb ending -ly: the same ending turns national into nationally and natural into naturally.
normal.cn: cultural 加副词词尾 -ly：同一词尾也把 national（民族的）变成 nationally（在全国范围内）、把 natural（自然的）变成 naturally（自然地）。

normal.en: The family runs culture, cultural, cultured, culturally, cross-culturally and socioculturally.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 culture（文化）、cultural（文化的）、cultured（有修养的）、culturally（文化上）、cross-culturally（跨文化地）、socioculturally（在社会文化层面上）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: culturally diverse, culturally appropriate, culturally sensitive, culturally bound.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：文化上多元、文化上合宜、对文化差异敏感、受文化束缚。

normal.en: The adverb answers the question in what respect, not where or when.
normal.cn: 这个副词回答的是「在哪个方面」，而不是「在哪里」或「在何时」。

normal.en: Culturally speaking is the spoken frame that announces the angle of the next claim.
normal.cn: culturally speaking（从文化角度来说）是口语框架，用来宣告下一句话的角度。

abstract.en: Picture two villages on opposite slopes singing the same rhythm at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两座山村位于相对的山坡，却在同一时刻唱出相同的节奏。

abstract.en: Picture a measuring stick laid not along distance but along shared habits.
abstract.cn: 想象一把量尺不是沿距离摆放，而是沿共同习惯摆放。

abstract.en: Picture a window that can be opened as a view or closed into a cage, depending on who holds it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇窗，既可以打开成视野，也可以合拢成笼子，取决于谁握着它。

examples.en: The two regions are culturally linked by a common festival calendar.
examples.cn: 这两个地区因共有的节庆日历而在文化上相连。

examples.en: A joke that is funny at home may be culturally offensive abroad.
examples.cn: 在本地说来好笑的笑话，到了国外可能触犯文化禁忌。

examples.en: Culturally speaking, the new shopping street has changed very little.
examples.cn: 从文化角度来说，这条新商业街改变的东西其实很少。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「靠它扯」加「里」——靠共同习俗把彼此扯在一起，还落到具体的层面里，就是「在文化上」。

root: 由 cultural 加英语副词词尾 -ly 构成；cultural 来自拉丁语 cultura「耕作、照料」加形容词词尾 -alis。副词词尾 -ly 源自古英语 -lice。colere 在拉丁语之前的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one question: on what axis, by what cause, in what manner and through what channel does culture shape a thing?
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个问题展开：文化沿哪条轴、以什么原因、用什么方式、通过什么渠道塑造一件事物？

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler laid across two cultures to show where they meet and where they differ.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把横放在两种文化之间的尺子，标出它们在哪里相接、在哪里分开。

branches.en: AXIS AND FRAME: the plain comparison and the spoken frame both announce culture as the angle of judgement.
branches.cn: 比较轴与框架：平实的比较与口语框架都在宣告文化是判断的角度。

branches.en: CAUSE AND CHANNEL: culture both shapes behaviour and carries it from one generation to the next.
branches.cn: 原因与渠道：文化既塑造行为，也把行为一代代传下去。

branches.en: LOCAL FITNESS: what fits one group's norms may fail another's.
branches.cn: 当地合宜：符合某一群体规范的做法，换一个群体可能就不合适。

branches.en: ARTISTIC RICHNESS: the axis narrows from the whole way of life to its works and ideas.
branches.cn: 艺术丰富度：比较轴从整套生活方式收窄到它的作品与思想。

branches.en: AWARENESS AND LIMIT: culture can be watched with care or turned into a blind cage.
branches.cn: 意识与局限：文化可以被小心观照，也可能变成看不见的笼子。

intro.en: Culturally is a chain of three pieces: a Latin noun stem, a Latin adjective ending and an English adverb ending.
intro.cn: culturally 由三段串成：拉丁名词词干、拉丁形容词词尾与英语副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin colere gives cultura, -alis makes it an adjective, and Old English -lice supplies the adverb ending that became modern -ly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 colere 给出 cultura，-alis 把它变成形容词，古英语 -lice 提供后来变成现代 -ly 的副词词尾。

items.structure: colere (Latin verb, to till or worship)
items.example: The stem also builds cultivate and colony.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干也构成 cultivate（耕作、培养）与 colony（聚居地）。

items.example: The noun became English culture through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词经法语成为英语 culture。

items.example: The same ending builds natural and national.
items.exampleCN: 同一词尾也构成 natural（自然的）与 national（民族的）。

items.example: The museum is a cultural institution.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆是一个文化机构。

items.structure: -lice (Old English adverb ending, from lic, body or form)
items.example: The ending turns quick into quickly.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 quick（快的）变成 quickly（快地）。

items.example: The two towns are culturally close.
items.exampleCN: 这两座镇在文化上很接近。

items.example: The team compared the results cross-culturally.
items.exampleCN: 团队对这些结果作了跨文化比较。

items.example: The practice is socioculturally specific.
items.exampleCN: 这一做法具有社会文化的特定性。

latinEntries.structure: colere, colui, cultum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
latinEntries.meaning: to till; to dwell; to worship

derivatives.meaning: in a way that spans cultures

definition_zh: 多元文化的；包含或代表多种文化的；由不同族裔群体组成的；（政策、教育）面向多种文化的
definition_en: containing, representing or designed for several different cultures
core_image: 同一条街上并排开着面包房、寺院与外语报摊，每一扇门里都传出不同的语言
scene: 清晨的街区里，面包房、寺院与小报摊挤在同一条街上，招牌上的字各不相同，The city is multicultural, with bakeries, temples and newspapers from a dozen communities.
sceneCN: 这里 multicultural 指「包含并代表多种文化的」（第 1 个义项：一个空间里共存多种文化）；句意为这座城市是多元文化的，一条街上就有十几个社群的面包房、寺院与报纸。图中可辨识物件：面包房橱窗、寺院门廊、报摊、不同文字的招牌。

pos.zh: 多元文化的；包含多种文化的；面向多种文化的

derivatives.zh: 多元文化主义；多元文化政策
多元文化主义者；多元文化主义的

senses.title: Containing several cultures in one place
senses.titleCN: 同一空间里包含多种文化
senses.definition: containing or representing several different cultures within one society or place
senses.definitionCN: 在同一社会或地点内包含或代表多种不同文化
senses.example: The city is multicultural, with bakeries, temples and newspapers from a dozen communities.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市是多元文化的，一条街上就有十几个社群的面包房、寺院与报纸。
senses.why: The prefix adds many to the adjective of culture: one place now holds several ways of life at once.
senses.whyCN: 前缀把「多」加到「文化的」形容词上：同一个地点同时容纳好几种生活方式。

senses.title: Designed for several cultural groups
senses.titleCN: 为多个文化群体而设计的
senses.definition: planned or organized so that people from different cultural backgrounds can take part
senses.definitionCN: 为使不同文化背景的人都能参与而规划或组织的
senses.example: The school runs a multicultural education programme in four languages.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校用四种语言开设多元文化教育项目。
senses.why: Once an institution must serve several groups, the adjective moves from describing a place to describing a design.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一个机构必须服务多个群体，这个形容词就从描述地点转为描述设计。

senses.title: Made up of people of different origins
senses.titleCN: 由不同族裔来源的人组成
senses.definition: having a population drawn from several ethnic or national origins
senses.definitionCN: 人口来自多个族裔或国家来源
senses.example: The ward is multicultural: half its residents were born abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 这个选区是多元文化的：一半居民在国外出生。
senses.why: This sense counts people rather than traditions: the mix is in the population, not necessarily in a policy.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项数的是人，而不是传统：混杂在人口里，不一定在政策里。

senses.title: Reflecting several cultures in content
senses.titleCN: 在内容上反映多种文化
senses.definition: including material, images or voices from several cultures in a curriculum, book or exhibition
senses.definitionCN: 在课程、书籍或展览中纳入多种文化的材料、图像或声音
senses.example: The anthology is multicultural, pairing poets from three continents.
senses.exampleCN: 这本选集是多元文化的，把三个大洲的诗人放在一起。
senses.why: Here the many cultures appear as content to be read or seen, so the adjective qualifies a work rather than a society.
senses.whyCN: 这里多种文化作为可读、可看的内容出现，因此这个形容词修饰的是一部作品，而不是一个社会。

senses.title: Characterized by coexistence of traditions
senses.titleCN: 以多种传统共存为特征
senses.definition: marked by the peaceful coexistence of distinct traditions in daily life
senses.definitionCN: 以不同传统在日常生活中和平共存为特征
senses.example: The old quarter is multicultural, with processions that pass each other without conflict.
senses.exampleCN: 老城区是多元文化的，不同的游行队伍彼此交错而过，并不冲突。
senses.why: The adjective can describe a rhythm of daily life, not just a count of groups: coexistence is the feature being named.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可描述日常生活的节奏，而不只是群体的数量：被命名的是「共存」这一特征。

senses.title: The official policy sense
senses.titleCN: 官方政策意义上的多元文化
senses.definition: relating to a state policy that officially recognizes and supports several cultures
senses.definitionCN: 与官方承认并支持多种文化的国家政策有关的
senses.example: Canada is often described as a multicultural state.
senses.exampleCN: 加拿大常被描述为多元文化国家。
senses.why: In this sense the adjective is a legal and political category, created when governments adopted multiculturalism as policy.
senses.whyCN: 在这个义项里，形容词是法律与政治范畴，是在政府把多元文化主义定为政策时才产生的。

senses.title: Mixing cultural forms in art
senses.titleCN: 艺术中混合多种文化形式
senses.definition: combining styles, genres or techniques drawn from different cultural traditions
senses.definitionCN: 把来自不同文化传统的风格、体裁或技法混合在一起
senses.example: Her multicultural collage joins calligraphy with electronic sound.
senses.exampleCN: 她的多元文化拼贴把书法与电子声音接在一起。
senses.why: The prefix can also work inside a work of art, where several traditions are deliberately placed side by side.
senses.whyCN: 这个前缀也可以在艺术品内部起作用，把好几种传统有意并置。

senses.title: Of a person formed by several cultures
senses.definition: describing a person whose upbringing or background has been shaped by more than one culture
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人的成长或背景受不止一种文化塑造
senses.example: She calls herself multicultural, cooking two cuisines and dreaming in two languages.
senses.exampleCN: 她说自己是多元文化的，会做两种菜系，也用两种语言做梦。
senses.why: The adjective can move from groups to one person: a single life may hold several cultural repertoires.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可以从群体移到个人：一条生命里可以装着好几套文化本领。

intro.en: Multicultural joins Latin multus, many, with cultural, from Latin cultura, tilling and care. The compound is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: multicultural 由拉丁语 multus「多」与 cultural 结合而成，而 cultural 来自拉丁语 cultura「耕作、照料」。这是个现代复合词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Multus meant much or many. Its combining form multi- entered English through French and Latin and attaches freely to adjectives and nouns.
items.cn: multus 意为「多的、许多的」。它的组合形式 multi- 经法语与拉丁语进入英语，可自由附着在形容词与名词上。

items.en: Cultura, tilling and care, came from colere, to till or worship; English culture and cultural descend from it.
items.cn: cultura 意为耕作与照料，来自 colere「耕种、敬拜」；英语 culture 与 cultural 都由此而来。

items.en: English speakers combined the many-prefix with cultural once migration had made several cultures visible in one society.
items.cn: 当移民让多种文化在同一社会中变得可见，英语使用者就把表示「多」的前缀与 cultural 组合起来。

items.en: In the later twentieth century the adjective became a policy word in Canada and Australia, where official multiculturalism was adopted.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，这个形容词在加拿大与澳大利亚成为政策用语，因为两地都采纳了官方的多元文化主义。

items.en: Schools, museums and critics then extended it to curricula, exhibitions and mixed artistic forms.
items.cn: 随后学校、博物馆与评论家又把它扩展到课程、展览与混合的艺术形式。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of the compound is dated differently, and the exact year when it became an official policy term is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个复合词在英语中的最早使用各家说法不一；它成为官方政策用语的确切年份也没有定论。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same stock that are often swapped; the second holds adjectives for mixing or variety.
note.cn: 第一组是同源、常被误换的词；第二组是表示混合或多样性的形容词。

entries.definition: The policy or ideology that supports several cultures; multicultural is the adjective describing a state or design.
entries.definitionCN: 支持多种文化的政策或意识形态；multicultural 是描述状态或设计的形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to culture in general or to one culture; it lacks the many-prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 与一般文化或某一种文化有关；它没有表示「多」的前缀。

entries.definition: Relating to interaction between cultures; multicultural describes several cultures coexisting inside one space.
entries.definitionCN: 与不同文化之间的互动有关；multicultural 描述多种文化在同一空间内共存。

entries.definition: Comparing or spanning cultures; it stresses the crossing, while multicultural stresses the mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 比较或跨越不同文化；它强调「跨越」，multicultural 强调「混合」。

entries.definition: Made up of several ethnic groups; it counts origins, while multicultural can also cover arts, policy and daily life.
entries.definitionCN: 由多个族裔群体组成；它数的是来源，而 multicultural 还可涵盖艺术、政策与日常生活。

entries.definition: Showing much variety of any kind; it does not specify that the variety is cultural.
entries.definitionCN: 显示出任何种类的丰富差异；它没有指明差异是文化上的。

entries.definition: Containing more than one element, often used of societies; it is broader and less specific than multicultural.
entries.definitionCN: 包含不止一个要素，常用于社会；比 multicultural 更宽、更不具体。

entries.definition: Made up of people and influences from many countries; it stresses international openness rather than internal cultural policy.
entries.definitionCN: 由许多国家的人与影响构成；它强调国际开放，而非内部文化政策。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real many-prefix, the real culture root and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「多」的真实前缀、真实的 culture 词根，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: multi- means many, as in multiple and multimillion; cultural means of culture, so the word says many cultures at once.
normal.cn: multi- 表示「多」，如 multiple（多个的）与 multimillion（数百万的）；cultural 表示「文化的」，所以这个词说的是同时有多种文化。

normal.en: The family runs multicultural, multiculturalism, multiculturalist and multiculturally.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 multicultural（多元文化的）、multiculturalism（多元文化主义）、multiculturalist（多元文化主义者）、multiculturally（以多元文化的方式）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: multicultural society, multicultural education, multicultural policy, multicultural background.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：多元文化社会、多元文化教育、多元文化政策、多元文化背景。

normal.en: The word came of age when migration made several cultures visible in one city.
normal.cn: 当移民让多种文化在同一座城市里变得可见，这个词才真正成熟。

normal.en: Contrast the three prefixes: multi- is many inside, inter- is between, cross- is across.
normal.cn: 对照三个前缀：multi- 指内部有多个，inter- 指彼此之间，cross- 指横跨而过。

abstract.en: Picture one street holding several kitchens, each with its own smell.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街上开着好几家厨房，每家都有自己的气味。

abstract.en: Picture a curriculum with several voices speaking at once, none of them drowned out.
abstract.cn: 想象一份课程里有好几个声音同时说话，没有一个被淹没。

abstract.en: Picture a person carrying two languages in one mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人一张嘴里装着两种语言。

examples.en: The library serves a multicultural neighbourhood with books in nine languages.
examples.cn: 这家图书馆服务一个多元文化的社区，藏书有九种语言。

examples.en: A multicultural curriculum does not replace the canon; it widens it.
examples.cn: 多元文化课程并不取代经典，而是把经典的范围拓宽。

examples.en: The festival is multicultural in its music, food and costumes.
examples.cn: 这个节庆在音乐、食物与服饰上都是多元文化的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多」加「文化的」——一个地方装下许多种文化，就是多元文化的。

root: 由拉丁语 multus「多」的组合形式 multi- 与 cultural 结合而成；cultural 来自拉丁语 cultura「耕作、照料」，再往前是 colere「耕种、敬拜」。这是现代英语复合词，colere 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one container: a place, a programme, a population, a text, a daily rhythm, a policy, an artwork and finally a single life all hold several cultures.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「容器」展开：地点、项目、人口、文本、日常节奏、政策、艺术品，最后连一条生命，都可以装着好几种文化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one street with several doors, each opening onto a different way of life.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条街上有好几扇门，每扇门后都是不同的生活方式。

branches.en: SPACE AND RHYTHM: several cultures share one place, and their traditions learn to pass one another without collision.
branches.cn: 空间与节奏：多种文化共享一个地点，它们的传统学会彼此交错而不相撞。

branches.en: DESIGN AND POLICY: a school programme and a state policy both organize the many cultures from above.
branches.cn: 设计与政策：学校的项目与国家的政策都从上方组织这多种文化。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the mixture can be counted in the population itself.
branches.cn: 人：这种混合可以直接在人口中数出来。

branches.en: CONTENT: a book or exhibition can hold the many cultures as material to be read and seen.
branches.cn: 内容：一本书或一场展览可以把多种文化作为可读、可看的材料装进去。

branches.en: MIXED FORMS AND LIVES: art can join traditions, and one person can carry several cultural repertoires.
branches.cn: 混合的形式与生命：艺术可以把传统接在一起，一个人也可以装着好几套文化本领。

intro.en: Multicultural is a many-prefix, a culture stem and an adjective ending, with further suffixes building the policy words.
intro.cn: multicultural 由一个表示「多」的前缀、一个 culture 词干与一个形容词词尾构成，后续词尾又造出政策类词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin multus supplies the many-prefix, cultura supplies the culture stem, and -alis supplies the adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 multus 提供表示「多」的前缀，cultura 提供 culture 词干，-alis 提供形容词词尾。

items.example: The stem also appears in multiple and multiply.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干也出现在 multiple（多个的）与 multiply（乘、增多）里。

items.example: The prefix builds multilingual and multiethnic.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀构成 multilingual（多语的）与 multiethnic（多族裔的）。

items.example: The noun became English culture through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词经法语成为英语 culture。

items.example: The ending builds cultural and natural.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 cultural（文化的）与 natural（自然的）。

items.example: The city is multicultural.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市是多元文化的。

items.meaning: the policy of supporting several cultures
items.meaningCN: 支持多种文化的政策或主义
items.example: The province adopted multiculturalism in the nineteen seventies.
items.exampleCN: 该省在二十世纪七十年代采纳了多元文化主义。

items.meaningCN: 多元文化主义的支持者
items.example: The multiculturalist defended the language programme.
items.exampleCN: 这位多元文化主义者为语言项目辩护。

items.example: The neighbourhood is multiculturally mixed.
items.exampleCN: 这个街区在文化上是混合的。

items.example: Scholars debate the multiculturality of the old port.
items.exampleCN: 学者们争论这座老港口的多元文化状态。

derivatives.meaning: the doctrine or policy of several cultures

derivatives.meaningCN: 多元文化主义的支持者

definition_zh: 多元文化主义；多种文化共存的状态；支持文化多样性的官方政策或意识形态
definition_en: the condition, policy or ideology in which several cultures coexist and are officially recognized
core_image: 一张长桌上并排放着好几本不同文字的同一份文件，每一本都盖着同样的公章
scene: 一份省级文件把多种文化共存写成官方立场，会议室里摆着好几种语言的译本，The province adopted multiculturalism as official policy in the nineteen seventies.
sceneCN: 这里 multiculturalism 指「以官方政策形式承认并支持多种文化的制度安排」（第 2 个义项：国家或省级政策）；句意为该省在二十世纪七十年代把多元文化主义定为官方政策。图中可辨识物件：长桌、多语译本、公章、政策文件。

senses.title: The coexistence of several cultures
senses.definition: the condition in which several cultures live side by side in one society
senses.definitionCN: 多种文化在同一社会中并存的状况
senses.example: Multiculturalism is a fact of the city before it is a policy.
senses.exampleCN: 在这座城市里，多元文化先是事实，然后才成为政策。
senses.why: The suffix turns the adjective into a noun of condition: what was a description of a place now names the state of that place.
senses.whyCN: 后缀把形容词变成表示状态的名词：原本描述地点的说法，现在命名那个地点的状态。

senses.title: An official policy supporting several cultures
senses.titleCN: 支持多种文化的官方政策
senses.definition: a government policy that recognizes and supports the cultures of different groups
senses.definitionCN: 承认并支持不同群体文化的政府政策
senses.example: The province adopted multiculturalism as official policy in the nineteen seventies.
senses.exampleCN: 该省在二十世纪七十年代把多元文化主义定为官方政策。
senses.why: Once a state funds language classes and heritage festivals, the condition becomes an instrument of government.
senses.whyCN: 一旦国家资助语言课程与遗产节庆，这种状态就变成治理工具。

senses.title: An ideology that values difference
senses.definition: the belief that cultural differences should be preserved and valued rather than melted away
senses.definitionCN: 认为文化差异应被保留和重视、而非被熔化的信念
senses.example: Multiculturalism insists that difference is a public good, not a problem to be solved.
senses.exampleCN: 多元文化主义坚持差异是一种公共善，而不是待解决的问题。
senses.why: Policy needs a theory behind it, so the same word also names the belief that gives the policy its justification.
senses.whyCN: 政策背后需要理论，因此同一个词也命名那套为政策提供理由的信念。

senses.title: A social movement for recognition
senses.definition: the movement through which minority groups seek public recognition of their cultures
senses.definitionCN: 少数群体争取其文化获得公共承认的运动
senses.example: Multiculturalism grew out of movements that demanded a place in the school curriculum.
senses.exampleCN: 多元文化主义源自那些要求在课程中占有一席之地的运动。
senses.why: The noun can name actors as well as ideas: people organized to make the condition visible and the policy possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既可指观念，也可指行动者：人们组织起来，让这种状态被看见，也让政策成为可能。

senses.title: An educational approach
senses.definition: an approach in schools that includes the histories and cultures of several groups
senses.definitionCN: 在学校中纳入多个群体历史与文化的教育取向
senses.example: Multiculturalism in the classroom changed which poets were read.
senses.exampleCN: 课堂里的多元文化主义改变了学生读哪些诗人的作品。
senses.why: Schools are where a society decides what the next generation will inherit, so the doctrine quickly becomes a curriculum question.
senses.whyCN: 学校是社会决定下一代继承什么的地方，因此这套主张很快变成课程问题。

senses.title: A demographic description
senses.definition: a neutral description of a society composed of several cultural groups
senses.definitionCN: 对由多个文化群体组成的社会的中性描述
senses.example: Census reports use multiculturalism to describe the changing suburbs.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查报告用多元文化主义来描述不断变化的郊区。
senses.why: The word can be stripped of ideology and used as a plain count: several cultures are present, and that is all it says.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以剥离意识形态，只作平实计数：这里存在多种文化，如此而已。

senses.title: A label used by critics
senses.definition: the word as used by opponents who blame it for fragmentation or for treating groups as separate
senses.definitionCN: 反对者用它指责社会碎片化、或把群体当作彼此隔离的标签
senses.example: The minister blamed multiculturalism for the decline of a shared public life.
senses.exampleCN: 这位部长把公共生活的衰退归咎于多元文化主义。
senses.why: A policy that protects difference can be accused of producing separation, so the same noun becomes a term of attack.
senses.whyCN: 保护差异的政策可能被指控制造隔阂，于是同一个名词变成攻击用语。

senses.title: Mixing traditions in art and media
senses.titleCN: 艺术与媒体中混合多种传统
senses.definition: an artistic practice that deliberately combines forms from several cultural traditions
senses.definitionCN: 有意把多种文化传统的形式结合起来的艺术实践
senses.example: The film's multiculturalism is visible in its mixed score and subtitles.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片的多元文化主义体现在混编配乐与字幕上。
senses.why: The doctrine of many cultures becomes a style when artists let traditions meet inside one work.
senses.whyCN: 当艺术家让多种传统在一件作品里相遇，这套「多文化」主张就变成一种风格。

intro.en: Multiculturalism is multicultural plus -ism, the suffix for doctrines and movements, which reached English through Latin from Greek. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: multiculturalism 是 multicultural 加 -ism 构成，后者是表示学说与运动的后缀，经拉丁语从希腊语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Multus, many, supplied the combining prefix multi-, which English uses freely in modern compounds.
items.cn: multus 意为「多」，提供组合前缀 multi-，英语在现代复合词中自由使用它。

items.en: Cultura, tilling and care, gave culture and cultural; the culture here is the learned way of life, not the field.
items.cn: cultura 意为耕作与照料，给出 culture 与 cultural；这里的 culture 指习得的生活方式，而非田地。

items.en: Greek -ismos named a practice or doctrine and passed through Latin -ismus into English -ism, which builds socialism, realism and multiculturalism alike.
items.cn: 希腊语 -ismos 指某种实践或学说，经拉丁语 -ismus 进入英语 -ism，同样构成 socialism（社会主义）、realism（写实主义）与 multiculturalism。

items.en: The noun appeared in the mid twentieth century as migration made several cultures a permanent public fact in industrial cities.
items.cn: 这个名词在二十世纪中叶出现，当时移民使多种文化成为工业城市里长期的公共事实。

items.en: Canada adopted an official multiculturalism policy in the early nineteen seventies, and Australia followed soon after, turning the word into a label of state policy.
items.cn: 加拿大在二十世纪七十年代初采纳官方多元文化政策，澳大利亚随后跟进，把这个词变成国家政策的标签。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of the noun and the exact date of its adoption as policy are reported differently, so both should be treated as approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个名词在英语中的最早使用、以及它被采纳为政策的确切日期，各家记载不一，两者都应视为约数。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same stock that are easily confused; the second holds doctrines or descriptions of plural societies.
note.cn: 第一组是同源、极易混淆的词；第二组是关于多元社会的学说或描述。

entries.definition: Describing a place or design that contains several cultures; multiculturalism is the noun for the condition, policy or doctrine.
entries.definitionCN: 描述包含多种文化的地点或设计；multiculturalism 是表示状态、政策或学说的名词。

entries.definition: A supporter of multiculturalism; the -ist form names a person, not the doctrine.
entries.definitionCN: 多元文化主义的支持者；带 -ist 的形式指人，不指学说。

entries.definition: An approach that explains human behaviour mainly by culture; it lacks the many-prefix and is not a policy label.
entries.definitionCN: 主要用文化解释人类行为的取向；它没有表示「多」的前缀，也不是政策标签。

entries.definition: A policy or approach stressing exchange and interaction between cultures rather than their parallel existence.
entries.definitionCN: 强调文化之间的交流与互动、而非平行共存的政策或取向。

entries.definition: The acceptance of many groups or viewpoints in one society; broader than multiculturalism, which focuses on culture.
entries.definitionCN: 接受一个社会中存在多个群体或观点；比聚焦文化的 multiculturalism 更宽。

entries.definition: The presence of variety; it can be cultural, biological or organizational, and carries no programme by itself.
entries.definitionCN: 存在多样性；可以是文化的、生物的和组织的，本身不携带纲领。

entries.definition: The view that all people belong to one worldwide community; it stresses openness to the world, not the protection of separate cultures.
entries.definitionCN: 认为所有人都属于同一个世界共同体的观点；它强调对世界开放，而非保护彼此分隔的文化。

entries.definition: The process by which minority groups are absorbed into the dominant culture; it is the policy multiculturalism often defines itself against.
entries.definitionCN: 少数群体被吸收进主流文化的过程；它常是多元文化主义用来定义自身对立面的政策。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real doctrine suffix, the real family and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示学说的真实后缀、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: multicultural plus the doctrine suffix: the same ending builds realism and socialism, so the word names a programme, not a count.
normal.cn: multicultural 加表示学说的后缀：同一词尾也构成 realism（写实主义）与 socialism（社会主义），因此这个词命名一套纲领，而不是一次计数。

normal.en: The family runs multicultural, multiculturalism, multiculturalist and multiculturalistic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 multicultural（多元文化的）、multiculturalism（多元文化主义）、multiculturalist（多元文化主义者）、multiculturalistic（带多元文化主义色彩的）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: official multiculturalism, state multiculturalism, the multiculturalism debate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：官方多元文化主义、国家多元文化主义、关于多元文化主义的争论。

normal.en: The word became official in Canada and Australia in the nineteen seventies.
normal.cn: 这个词在二十世纪七十年代于加拿大与澳大利亚成为官方用语。

normal.en: Its usual rival in policy debate is assimilation, not diversity.
normal.cn: 在政策争论中，它通常的对手是同化，而不是多样性。

abstract.en: Picture several books of law bound in one cover, each in a different script.
abstract.cn: 想象好几本法律文本装进同一个封面，每本用不同文字。

abstract.en: Picture a choir in which every section sings a different melody and none is asked to stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱团，每个声部唱不同旋律，却没有一个被要求停下。

abstract.en: Picture a map with many coloured regions and no single colour allowed to cover the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上有许多色块，没有任何一种颜色被允许盖满整页。

examples.en: Multiculturalism changed the language of citizenship in the late twentieth century.
examples.cn: 多元文化主义在二十世纪后期改变了公民身份的话语。

examples.en: The city's multiculturalism is older than its official policy.
examples.cn: 这座城市的多元文化比它的官方政策更早存在。

examples.en: Critics argue that multiculturalism can harden the boundaries it meant to soften.
examples.cn: 批评者认为，多元文化主义可能反而硬化了它本想软化的边界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多」加「文化的」再加「主义」——把许多种文化共存写成一套主张，就是多元文化主义。

root: 由 multicultural 加表示学说与运动的后缀 -ism 构成。multi- 来自拉丁语 multus「多」，cultural 来自拉丁语 cultura「耕作、照料」，-ism 经拉丁语 -ismus 源自希腊语 -ismos。colere 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one doctrine through its life: a condition, a policy, an ideology, a movement, a school subject, a census line, a term of attack and finally an artistic style.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一套主张的生命史展开：先是状态，再是政策、意识形态、运动、学校课程、人口普查条目、攻击用语，最后是艺术风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several scripts sharing one seal, each text officially equal.
core.cn: 核心意象：几种文字共享同一枚印章，每份文本在官方意义上平等。

branches.en: FACT AND COUNT: coexistence can be described neutrally, as a census describes a population.
branches.cn: 事实与计数：共存可以被中性描述，就像人口普查描述人口那样。

branches.en: POLICY: the state turns coexistence into budgets, language classes and heritage festivals.
branches.cn: 政策：国家把共存变成预算、语言课程与遗产节庆。

branches.en: DOCTRINE AND MOVEMENT: a belief justifies the policy, and organized groups push it forward.
branches.cn: 学说与运动：信念为政策提供理由，组织起来的群体则推动它。

branches.en: SCHOOLING: the curriculum decides which cultures the next generation will inherit.
branches.cn: 学校教育：课程决定下一代继承哪些文化。

branches.en: ATTACK AND STYLE: opponents turn the word into blame, while artists turn it into mixed forms.
branches.cn: 攻击与风格：反对者把这个词变成指责，艺术家则把它变成混合形式。

intro.en: Multiculturalism is a many-prefix, a culture stem, an adjective ending and a doctrine suffix in one word.
intro.cn: multiculturalism 由一个表示「多」的前缀、一个 culture 词干、一个形容词词尾与一个表示学说的后缀组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin multus and cultura supply the first two parts, -alis makes the adjective, and -ismus, from Greek -ismos, makes the doctrine noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 multus 与 cultura 提供前两部分，-alis 构成形容词，来自希腊语 -ismos 的 -ismus 则构成表示学说的名词。

items.structure: multi- (Latin combining form of multus, many)
items.example: The prefix also builds multilingual and multiethnic.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀也构成 multilingual（多语的）与 multiethnic（多族裔的）。

items.example: The noun became English culture through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词经法语成为英语 culture。

items.example: The ending builds cultural and natural.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 cultural（文化的）与 natural（自然的）。

items.example: The city is multicultural.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市是多元文化的。

items.example: The same ending builds realism and socialism.
items.exampleCN: 同一词尾也构成 realism（写实主义）与 socialism（社会主义）。

items.meaning: the policy or doctrine of several cultures
items.meaningCN: 多种文化的政策或学说
items.example: Official multiculturalism began in the nineteen seventies.
items.exampleCN: 官方多元文化主义始于二十世纪七十年代。

items.meaningCN: 多元文化主义的支持者
items.example: The multiculturalist defended the policy.
items.exampleCN: 这位多元文化主义者为政策辩护。

items.meaningCN: 带多元文化主义色彩的
items.example: The report has a multiculturalistic tone.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告带有多元文化主义的语调。

items.meaning: a doctrine stressing exchange between cultures
items.meaningCN: 强调文化间交流的学说
items.example: Interculturalism stresses dialogue more than parallel lives.
items.exampleCN: 跨文化主义更强调对话，而非平行生活。
