definition_zh: 文化遗产；世代相传的传统、价值观与实物；受保护的历史建筑与遗址；（法律、政策中的）文化遗产类别
definition_en: the traditions, objects and sites that a society inherits from earlier generations and passes on
core_image: 山谷里的老石屋被一块块补回原样，墙缝里夹着几代人写下的名字
scene: 山谷里的老屋由石匠一块块补回原样，账本上记着每面墙的年代，The trust repairs buildings that belong to the cultural heritage of the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 cultural heritage 指「由先辈留下、需要保护的实物与建筑」（第 2 个义项：物质文化遗产）；句意为该信托机构修缮属于山谷文化遗产的建筑。图中可辨识物件：石墙、脚手架、旧账本、刻字的门楣。

pos.zh: 文化遗产；世代相传的传统与实物；受保护的历史建筑与遗址

forms.label: 复数（多种文化遗产，少见）

senses.title: Traditions and values handed down
senses.titleCN: 世代相传的传统与价值观
senses.definition: the customs, beliefs, stories and values that a community receives from earlier generations
senses.definitionCN: 社群从先辈那里接受的习俗、信念、故事与价值观
senses.example: The songs sung at weddings are part of the cultural heritage of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼上唱的歌谣是这座山谷文化遗产的一部分。
senses.why: Heritage begins as a handover: what matters is not the object but the fact that one generation gives it to the next.
senses.whyCN: 遗产起初是一种交接：重要的不是物件本身，而是一代人把它交给下一代这一事实。

senses.title: Physical objects, buildings and sites
senses.definition: the material remains, monuments and historic places that a society inherits
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会继承下来的实物遗存、纪念物与历史场所
senses.example: The trust repairs buildings that belong to the cultural heritage of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托机构修缮属于山谷文化遗产的建筑。
senses.why: The handover image becomes concrete: a wall, a tool or a street can outlive the hands that made it.
senses.whyCN: 交接的意象变得具体：一面墙、一件工具或一条街，可以比造它的手活得更久。

senses.title: An official or legal category
senses.definition: the status given by law or international convention to objects and places judged worth protecting
senses.definitionCN: 法律或国际公约赋予那些被认为值得保护的物件与场所的地位
senses.example: The old town was listed as cultural heritage, which froze the plans for a new road.
senses.exampleCN: 老城被列为文化遗产，这使新路的规划停了下来。
senses.why: Once a list exists, heritage becomes a legal status: a building is not merely old but protected, with duties attached.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有了名录，遗产就成为法律地位：一栋建筑不只是旧，而是受保护，并附带义务。

senses.title: The shared legacy that forms identity
senses.definition: the body of inherited culture through which a group recognizes itself
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体借以认出自身的继承文化总体
senses.example: The language is the most durable part of their cultural heritage.
senses.exampleCN: 语言是他们文化遗产中最持久的部分。
senses.why: Heritage tells a group what it has in common with its dead, and that continuity is what identity is made of.
senses.whyCN: 遗产告诉一个群体它与逝者共有何物，而认同正是由这种连续性构成的。

senses.title: A field of study and management
senses.definition: the professional work of recording, conserving and interpreting inherited culture
senses.definitionCN: 记录、保护与阐释继承文化的专业工作
senses.example: Cultural heritage management decides which ruins to keep and which to let fall.
senses.exampleCN: 文化遗产管理决定哪些废墟保留、哪些任其倒塌。
senses.why: Heritage needs experts because keeping something costs money and involves choices that pure sentiment cannot make.
senses.whyCN: 遗产需要专家，因为保存要花钱，还要做出单凭感情无法作出的选择。

senses.title: Heritage as tourism and industry
senses.titleCN: 作为旅游与产业的遗产
senses.definition: inherited culture marketed as an attraction for visitors
senses.definitionCN: 被包装成游客吸引物的继承文化
senses.example: Cultural heritage pays for the roof repairs, but it also fills the square with buses.
senses.exampleCN: 文化遗产付得起屋顶修缮费，却也让广场停满大巴。
senses.why: The same handover can be sold: visitors pay to see what earlier generations left, and the money changes the place.
senses.whyCN: 同一种交接也可以出售：游客付费看先辈留下的东西，而钱又改变了这个地方。

senses.title: Family and community memory
senses.definition: the private or local memory, language and stories that a family or small community passes on
senses.definitionCN: 家庭或小社群传递的私人或地方记忆、语言与故事
senses.example: Her grandmother's recipes are cultural heritage at the scale of one kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母的菜谱是只属于一间厨房的文化遗产。
senses.why: Heritage does not require a monument: a recipe, a dialect or a name can be handed down with the same care.
senses.whyCN: 遗产不一定需要纪念碑：一张菜谱、一种方言或一个名字，也可以用同样的心意传下去。

senses.title: Digital heritage
senses.definition: inherited culture recorded, stored or reconstructed in digital form
senses.definitionCN: 以数字形式记录、保存或重建的继承文化
senses.example: The archive's cultural heritage now includes scans of every clay tablet.
senses.exampleCN: 该档案馆的文化遗产如今包括每一块泥板的扫描件。
senses.why: When the record itself becomes the thing kept, heritage moves from stone to server without losing the handover.
senses.whyCN: 当记录本身成为被保存之物，遗产就从石头移到服务器，而交接并没有消失。

intro.en: Cultural heritage joins cultural, from Latin cultura, with heritage, from Latin heres, heir, through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cultural heritage 由 cultural 与 heritage 结合而成；cultural 来自拉丁语 cultura，heritage 经法语来自拉丁语 heres「继承人」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Heres meant heir. Its deeper origin is source uncertain; it is not securely connected to any other Latin root.
items.cn: heres 意为「继承人」。它更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠地联系到任何其他拉丁词根。

items.en: Hereditare meant to inherit or to leave by will, built on the noun for heir and its stem hered-.
items.cn: hereditare 意为「继承、按遗嘱留下」，由表示继承人的名词及其词干 hered- 构成。

items.en: Old French eritage named an inherited estate and passed into Middle English as heritage.
items.cn: 古法语 eritage 指继承得来的产业，后进入中古英语，成为 heritage。

items.en: English heritage first meant inherited property and later widened to customs, language and shared past.
items.cn: 英语 heritage 最初指继承的财产，后来扩展到习俗、语言与共有的过去。

items.en: Cultural heritage became a standard term in the twentieth century as states and international bodies began listing what should be protected.
items.cn: 随着国家与国际机构开始编制应受保护的名录，cultural heritage 在二十世纪成为标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of the full phrase is not securely dated, and the origin of heres remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：完整短语在英语中的最早使用没有确切年代；heres 的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the heir root; the second holds terms for inherited culture with a different emphasis.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在「继承人」词根上的词；第二组是强调重点不同的继承文化术语。

entries.definition: Inherited property or tradition in general; cultural heritage specifies that the inheritance is cultural rather than financial.
entries.definitionCN: 一般意义上的继承财产或传统；cultural heritage 指明继承的是文化而非财物。

entries.definition: To receive property, traits or traditions from a predecessor; it names the act, while the phrase names what is received.
entries.definitionCN: 从前人那里接受财产、性状或传统；它指动作，而短语指所接受之物。

entries.definition: The property or traits received, especially in law or genetics; it is narrower and more technical than cultural heritage.
entries.definitionCN: 所接受的财产或性状，尤其在法律或遗传学中；它比 cultural heritage 更窄、更技术化。

entries.definition: Transmitted from parent to child, especially of titles or disease; it stresses biological or legal descent, not culture.
entries.definitionCN: 由父母传给子女，尤其指头衔或疾病；它强调生理或法律传承，而非文化。

entries.definition: Something handed down from a predecessor, often with a personal or historical tone; cultural heritage is the collective and public version.
entries.definitionCN: 前人留下之物，常带个人或历史语气；cultural heritage 是集体、公共的版本。

entries.definition: An inheritance from ancestors, often used of national or religious property; more formal and more legal than cultural heritage.
entries.definitionCN: 祖先传下的遗产，常用于国家或宗教财产；比 cultural heritage 更正式、更法律化。

entries.definition: A custom or belief passed down by practice; tradition is one part of cultural heritage, not the whole collection.
entries.definitionCN: 通过实践传下的习俗或信念；传统是文化遗产的一部分，而非全部。

entries.definition: In law, movable or immovable objects of cultural value; it is the legal counterpart of the broader cultural heritage.
entries.definitionCN: 法律上具有文化价值的可动或不可动物件；它是更宽的 cultural heritage 在法律上的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real heir root, the real family and the phrases the term actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「继承人」词根、真实的同族词，以及这个术语实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: heritage comes from the word for heir: what is handed to the next generation is an inheritance.
normal.cn: heritage 来自表示「继承人」的词：交给下一代的东西就是一份继承。

normal.en: The family runs heritage, inherit, inheritance, hereditary and inheritor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 heritage（遗产）、inherit（继承）、inheritance（继承、遗产）、hereditary（世袭的、遗传的）、inheritor（继承人）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: cultural heritage site, intangible cultural heritage, cultural heritage management.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：文化遗产地、非物质文化遗产、文化遗产管理。

normal.en: The phrase covers both songs and stone: not everything inherited is an object.
normal.cn: 这个短语既包括歌谣，也包括石头：并非所有被继承的东西都是物件。

normal.en: Its legal twin is cultural property, which is narrower and protects objects.
normal.cn: 它在法律上的对应词是 cultural property（文化财产），后者更窄，保护的是物件。

abstract.en: Picture a handover across a generation, with one pair of hands letting go as another closes.
abstract.cn: 想象一次跨代的交接：一双手松开，另一双手合拢。

abstract.en: Picture a wall made of stones that each carry a different name.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙，每块石头上都刻着不同的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a song written on a clay tablet and also saved on a server.
abstract.cn: 想象一首歌既写在泥板上，也保存在服务器里。

examples.en: The language school treats the dialect as living cultural heritage, not a museum piece.
examples.cn: 这所语言学校把方言当作活的文化遗产，而不是博物馆展品。

examples.en: Cultural heritage law can protect a street better than it protects the people who live there.
examples.cn: 文化遗产法保护一条街的能力，可能胜过保护住在那里的人。

examples.en: The digital archive makes cultural heritage available to schools across the province.
examples.cn: 数字档案让全省的学校都能接触文化遗产。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「文化的」加「遗产」——先辈传下来的歌谣、老屋与手艺，就是文化遗产。

root: 由 cultural 与 heritage 组成。cultural 来自拉丁语 cultura「耕作、照料」，再往前是 colere「耕种、敬拜」；heritage 经古法语 eritage 来自拉丁语 heres「继承人」，更早的 hered- 词干与 hereditas「继承」相关，而 heres 的来源本身不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one handover: traditions, objects, legal status, identity, management, tourism, family memory and finally the digital record.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次交接展开：传统、实物、法律地位、认同、管理、旅游、家庭记忆，最后是数字记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand letting go of a stone while another hand closes around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手松开石头，另一只手合拢接住。

branches.en: INTANGIBLE AND PRIVATE: songs, recipes and dialects are handed down in kitchens and villages, not only in museums.
branches.cn: 无形与私人：歌谣、菜谱与方言在厨房和村庄里传下，不只在博物馆里。

branches.en: MATERIAL: walls and tools outlive their makers and become the visible part of the handover.
branches.cn: 物质：墙与工具比制作者活得更久，成为交接中可见的部分。

branches.en: STATUS AND IDENTITY: a listing turns an old place into a protected category, and a shared past into a group's image of itself.
branches.cn: 地位与认同：名录把一处旧地变成受保护的类别，也把共有的过去变成一个群体的自我形象。

branches.en: MANAGEMENT: experts decide what to keep, what to repair and what to let fall.
branches.cn: 管理：专家决定保留什么、修缮什么、任其倒塌什么。

branches.en: SALE AND SCAN: heritage can be sold to visitors or stored as data, but the handover remains.
branches.cn: 出售与扫描：遗产可以卖给游客，也可以存为数据，但交接仍在。

intro.en: Cultural heritage is a culture adjective plus an inheritance noun, and the inheritance noun has its own family.
intro.cn: cultural heritage 是一个文化形容词加一个继承名词，而这个继承名词又有自己的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres, heir, gives the hered- stem behind heritage, inherit and hereditary; cultura gives cultural.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 heres「继承人」给出 heritage、inherit 与 hereditary 背后的 hered- 词干；cultura 给出 cultural。

items.structure: heres, heredis (m./f., third declension, Latin noun)
items.example: The stem hered- runs through heritage and hereditary.
items.exampleCN: hered- 词干贯穿 heritage 与 hereditary。

items.example: The Latin noun named both the act and the property.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词既指继承行为，也指继承的财产。

items.meaning: to inherit; to leave by will
items.example: The verb produced French hériter and English inherit.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词产生了法语 hériter 与英语 inherit。

items.example: The house is part of the family heritage.
items.exampleCN: 这所房子是家族遗产的一部分。

items.example: She inherited the workshop from her uncle.
items.exampleCN: 她从叔叔那里继承了这间作坊。

items.example: The inheritance included the orchard.
items.exampleCN: 这份遗产包括那座果园。

items.meaning: passed by blood or by legal descent
items.meaningCN: 由血统或法定世系传下的
items.example: The title was hereditary.
items.exampleCN: 这个头衔是世袭的。

items.example: The noun gave English culture and cultural.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词给出英语 culture 与 cultural。

items.example: The ending builds cultural and natural.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 cultural（文化的）与 natural（自然的）。

latinEntries.meaning: to inherit; to leave by will

definition_zh: 遗产；继承的财产；世代相传的传统与文化；出身与天赋权利；历史遗迹与自然遗产
definition_en: property, traditions or culture passed down from earlier generations
core_image: 阁楼上那台旧织机蒙着布，几代人搬了几次家都没舍得丢
scene: 阁楼上那台旧织机蒙着布，几代人搬了几次家都没舍得丢，The family keeps the loom as part of its heritage.
sceneCN: 这里 heritage 指「从先辈继承下来、代代保留的财物」（第 1 个义项：继承的财产）；句意为这家人把那台织机当作遗产的一部分保留下来。图中可辨识物件：蒙布的织机、木楼梯、旧箱子、系着标签的钥匙。

pos.zh: 遗产；继承的财产；世代相传的传统与文化；历史遗迹

senses.title: Property inherited from ancestors
senses.definition: money, land or objects received from a predecessor, especially within a family
senses.definitionCN: 从前人、尤指家族成员那里接受的金钱、土地或物件
senses.example: The family keeps the loom as part of its heritage.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人把那台织机当作遗产的一部分保留下来。
senses.why: The oldest sense is legal and material: heritage is what passes to an heir when an owner dies.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是法律与物质上的：遗产是业主去世后传给继承人的东西。

senses.title: Traditions and values passed down
senses.titleCN: 世代相传的传统与价值观
senses.definition: customs, beliefs, stories and skills handed from one generation to the next
senses.definitionCN: 一代代传下的习俗、信念、故事与技艺
senses.example: The village's heritage lives in its songs more than in its buildings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄的遗产更多活在歌谣里，而不是建筑里。
senses.why: The legal handover is reused for culture: what is passed down may be a way of doing things rather than a deed.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的交接被挪用到文化上：传下来的可能是做事的方式，而不是一纸契据。

senses.title: Birthright and inherited status
senses.titleCN: 与生俱来的权利与继承的身份
senses.definition: the rights, rank or identity one holds by birth or family line
senses.definitionCN: 因出生或家族世系而拥有的权利、等级或身份
senses.example: She wears the ring as a sign of her heritage, not of her wealth.
senses.exampleCN: 她戴这枚戒指，表示的是她的出身，而不是财富。
senses.why: Heritage can be intangible in a social sense: a name or a rank arrives without any object changing hands.
senses.whyCN: 遗产在社会意义上可以是无形的：一个姓氏或一个等级到手时，并没有任何物件易手。

senses.title: Built heritage
senses.definition: historic buildings, monuments and townscapes valued as a collective inheritance
senses.definitionCN: 被当作集体继承物而珍视的历史建筑、纪念物与城镇景观
senses.example: The trust lists the mill as built heritage and forbids its demolition.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托机构把磨坊列为建筑遗产，禁止拆除。
senses.why: When a whole society inherits a building, the private word becomes public and legal.
senses.whyCN: 当整个社会继承一栋建筑，这个私人词汇就变成公共与法律用语。

senses.title: Natural heritage
senses.definition: landscapes, habitats and species treated as an inheritance worth protecting
senses.definitionCN: 被当作值得保护的继承物来对待的景观、栖息地与物种
senses.example: The valley's natural heritage includes the old orchard varieties.
senses.exampleCN: 这座山谷的自然遗产包括那些古老的果树品种。
senses.why: Heritage can be extended to what no human made: a landscape is inherited too, and can be lost like a building.
senses.whyCN: 遗产可以扩展到并非人造之物：一片景观也是继承来的，也会像建筑一样失去。

senses.title: The roots that shape identity
senses.definition: the inherited culture through which a person or group understands who they are
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或群体借以理解自身身份来源的继承文化
senses.example: He returned to the old quarter to recover a heritage he had never learned.
senses.exampleCN: 他回到老城区，想找回一份自己从未学过的遗产。
senses.why: Heritage answers the question where do I come from, so it becomes a resource for identity rather than a possession.
senses.whyCN: 遗产回答「我从哪里来」，因此它成为认同的资源，而非一件所有物。

senses.title: Heritage as tourism and industry
senses.titleCN: 作为旅游与产业的遗产
senses.definition: inherited places and traditions packaged and sold as visitor attractions
senses.definitionCN: 被包装并作为游客吸引物出售的继承场所与传统
senses.example: The heritage industry restored the harbour and then raised the ticket price.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产产业修复了港口，随后提高了票价。
senses.why: A public inheritance needs money to survive, and selling access to it creates a business with its own interests.
senses.whyCN: 公共继承物需要钱才能存活，而出售接近它的权利，就造出一个有自身利益的产业。

senses.title: The legacy of a movement or era
senses.titleCN: 一场运动或一个时代的遗泽
senses.definition: the achievements or consequences that later people receive from an earlier movement or period
senses.definitionCN: 后来者从较早的运动或时期那里继承的成就或后果
senses.example: Public libraries are part of the heritage of the reform movement.
senses.exampleCN: 公共图书馆是那场改革运动的遗泽之一。
senses.why: The family image widens one last time: a generation can inherit not only from relatives but from a struggle it never joined.
senses.whyCN: 家族的意象最后一次被放宽：一代人不仅可以从亲属那里继承，也可以从一场自己未曾参与的抗争中继承。

intro.en: Heritage comes through Old French from Late Latin hereditare, to inherit, built on Latin heres, heir. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: heritage 经古法语来自晚期拉丁语 hereditare「继承」，后者由拉丁语 heres「继承人」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Heres meant heir. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and it is not securely linked to another Latin root.
items.cn: heres 意为「继承人」。它更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠地联系到另一个拉丁词根。

items.en: Hereditare, to inherit or to leave by will, was formed on the hered- stem of heres and its noun hereditas, inheritance.
items.cn: hereditare 意为「继承或按遗嘱留下」，由 heres 的词干 hered- 及其名词 hereditas「继承」构成。

items.en: Old French eritage named an inherited estate; the h was restored in English spelling under Latin influence.
items.cn: 古法语 eritage 指继承的产业；英语拼写受拉丁语影响又补回了 h。

items.en: Middle English heritage first meant inherited property and the right to inherit it.
items.cn: 中古英语 heritage 最初指继承的财产以及继承它的权利。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word widened from private property to the shared past of a people, and later to buildings and landscapes.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，这个词从私人财产扩展到民族共有的过去，后来又扩展到建筑与景观。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of the cultural sense is not securely dated, and the origin of heres remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：文化义在英语中的最早使用没有确切年代；heres 的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds words from the heir root that differ in word class; the second holds near synonyms for what is passed down.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「继承人」词根、但词性不同的词；第二组是表示「传下之物」的近义词。

entries.definition: To receive property, traits or traditions from a predecessor; heritage is the noun for what is received.
entries.definitionCN: 从前人那里接受财产、性状或传统；heritage 是表示所接受之物的名词。

entries.definition: The property or traits received, especially in law or genetics; heritage is broader and often cultural.
entries.definitionCN: 所接受的财产或性状，尤其在法律或遗传学中；heritage 更宽，常指文化。

entries.definition: Passed from parent to child by blood or legal line; it describes the route of transmission, not the thing transmitted.
entries.definitionCN: 由血统或法定世系从父母传给子女；它描述传递路径，而非传递之物。

entries.definition: Capable of being inherited, used of property or traits; it is a technical adjective, not the noun heritage.
entries.definitionCN: 可被继承的，用于财产或性状；它是技术性形容词，不是名词 heritage。

entries.definition: Something handed down, often with a personal or historical tone; heritage is more collective and more official.
entries.definitionCN: 前人留下之物，常带个人或历史语气；heritage 更集体、更官方。

entries.definition: An inheritance from ancestors, especially national or religious property; it is more formal and more legal than heritage.
entries.definitionCN: 祖先传下的遗产，尤指国家或宗教财产；比 heritage 更正式、更法律化。

entries.definition: A custom or belief passed down by repeated practice; it is one kind of heritage, not its whole body.
entries.definitionCN: 通过反复实践传下的习俗或信念；它是遗产的一种，而非全部。

entries.definition: A right or property one holds from birth; it stresses entitlement, while heritage stresses the handover.
entries.definitionCN: 因出生而拥有的权利或财产；它强调应得资格，而 heritage 强调交接。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real heir root, the real family and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「继承人」词根、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: heritage shares the hered- stem with inherit and inheritance: all point to a handover to an heir.
normal.cn: heritage 与 inherit（继承）、inheritance（继承、遗产）共享 hered- 词干：都指向把东西交给继承人。

normal.en: The family runs heritage, inherit, inheritance, hereditary, heritable and inheritor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 heritage（遗产）、inherit（继承）、inheritance（继承、遗产）、hereditary（世袭的）、heritable（可继承的）、inheritor（继承人）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: national heritage, world heritage, heritage site, heritage industry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：国家遗产、世界遗产、遗产地、遗产产业。

normal.en: The word moved from a private will to a public past, then to buildings and landscapes.
normal.cn: 这个词从一份私人遗嘱移到公共的过去，再移到建筑与景观。

normal.en: A useful contrast: inheritance is legal and technical, while heritage is cultural and collective.
normal.cn: 有用的对照：inheritance 是法律与技术用语，而 heritage 是文化与集体用语。

abstract.en: Picture a trunk in an attic, labelled not with a name but with a generation.
abstract.cn: 想象阁楼上的一只箱子，标签上写的不是名字，而是一代人。

abstract.en: Picture a key that opens a door its owner has never seen.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙，打开一扇它的主人从未见过的门。

abstract.en: Picture a river that carries the silt of fields no living farmer ploughed.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河，载着在世农夫从未犁过的田地的泥沙。

examples.en: The museum treats the dialect recordings as heritage rather than as data.
examples.cn: 博物馆把方言录音当作遗产，而不是数据。

examples.en: World heritage status brought money and also brought crowds.
examples.cn: 世界遗产地位带来了钱，也带来了人潮。

examples.en: Heritage is not only what survives; it is what someone chooses to hand on.
examples.cn: 遗产不只是幸存下来的东西；它是有人选择传下去的东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喝瑞替吉」听成「喝了记得」——先辈留下的老屋与歌谣，喝了水也要记得，就是遗产。

root: 经古法语 eritage 来自晚期拉丁语 hereditare「继承」，后者由拉丁语 heres「继承人」及其词干 hered- 构成，并与 hereditas「继承」同族。heres 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one handover: property, traditions, status, built places, natural places, identity, tourism and finally the legacy of a movement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次交接展开：财产、传统、身份、建筑、自然场所、认同、旅游，最后是一场运动的遗泽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object passed from a dying hand to a living one, with no receipt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件东西从将逝的手交到活着的手里，没有收据。

branches.en: PRIVATE INHERITANCE: property and status pass to an heir, whether or not any object changes hands.
branches.cn: 私人继承：财产与身份传给继承人，无论是否有物件易手。

branches.en: CULTURE: songs, skills and beliefs are inherited like an estate.
branches.cn: 文化：歌谣、技艺与信念像产业一样被继承。

branches.en: BUILT: a whole society becomes the heir of a building.
branches.cn: 建筑：整个社会成为一栋建筑的继承人。

branches.en: NATURAL: landscapes are inherited too and can be lost like buildings.
branches.cn: 自然：景观也是继承来的，也会像建筑一样失去。

branches.en: IDENTITY, INDUSTRY AND MOVEMENT: heritage becomes roots, then a business, then the legacy of a struggle.
branches.cn: 认同、产业与运动：遗产先成为根，再成为生意，最后成为一场抗争的遗泽。

intro.en: Heritage is built on a Latin stem for heir, and that stem also produces inherit, inheritance and hereditary.
intro.cn: heritage 建立在表示「继承人」的拉丁词干上，这个词干还产生 inherit、inheritance 与 hereditary。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres, heir, and hereditas, inheritance, supply the hered- stem; Late Latin hereditare gives the verb that French turned into eritage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 heres「继承人」与 hereditas「继承」提供 hered- 词干；晚期拉丁语 hereditare 给出动词，法语又把它变成 eritage。

items.example: The stem hered- runs through the whole family.
items.exampleCN: hered- 词干贯穿整个词族。

items.example: The noun named both the act and the property.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指继承行为，也指继承的财产。

items.meaning: to inherit; to leave by will
items.example: French hériter and English inherit both descend from it.
items.exampleCN: 法语 hériter 与英语 inherit 都由此而来。

items.example: The loom is family heritage.
items.exampleCN: 这台织机是家族遗产。

items.example: She inherited the house.
items.exampleCN: 她继承了这所房子。

items.example: The inheritance was divided among four children.
items.exampleCN: 遗产分给了四个孩子。

items.example: The office was hereditary.
items.exampleCN: 这个职位是世袭的。

items.example: The land is heritable under the old law.
items.exampleCN: 按旧法，这片土地可以继承。

items.meaning: the passing of traits from parents
items.example: Heredity explains part of the pattern.
items.exampleCN: 遗传解释了这一模式的一部分。

latinEntries.meaning: to inherit; to leave by will

definition_zh: 传统主义；尊奉传统、抵制骤变的立场；宗教、政治、艺术或教育上的守成主张
definition_en: the attitude or doctrine that values inherited tradition and resists rapid change
core_image: 祠堂里那张磨得发亮的木板凳，年轻人想换新椅，老人却把旧的修了又修
scene: 祠堂里的木板凳磨得发亮，年轻人想换新椅，老人却把旧的修了又修，His traditionalism shows in the old songs he refuses to replace.
sceneCN: 这里 traditionalism 指「尊奉传统、不愿以新替旧的立场」（第 1 个义项：对既有方式的坚持）；句意为他的传统主义体现在那些他拒绝替换的旧歌里。图中可辨识物件：磨亮的板凳、修补的榫卯、旧歌本、年轻人的新椅图样。

pos.zh: 传统主义；尊奉传统的立场或主张

derivatives.zh: 传统主义者；传统主义的

senses.title: Adherence to established ways
senses.definition: the attitude of preferring inherited customs and practices to new ones
senses.definitionCN: 宁愿保留继承的习俗与实践、而不愿采用新方式的态度
senses.example: His traditionalism shows in the old songs he refuses to replace.
senses.exampleCN: 他的传统主义体现在那些他拒绝替换的旧歌里。
senses.why: The suffix names a stance rather than a habit: tradition is what is received, and traditionalism is the decision to keep receiving it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀命名一种立场，而非习惯：传统是被接受的东西，传统主义则是决定继续接受它。

senses.title: A conservative philosophy
senses.definition: a doctrine that treats inherited institutions as wiser than individual plans
senses.definitionCN: 认为继承而来的制度比个人计划更明智的学说
senses.example: Traditionalism argues that a custom surviving centuries has passed a test no reformer can repeat.
senses.exampleCN: 传统主义主张，延续数百年的习俗已经通过了一场改革者无法重做的检验。
senses.why: Once the preference becomes an argument, it turns into a philosophy: age itself is treated as evidence of fitness.
senses.whyCN: 当这种偏好变成论证，它就转为哲学：年岁本身被当作合宜性的证据。

senses.title: Religious traditionalism
senses.definition: the movement that keeps older forms of worship, doctrine or discipline
senses.definitionCN: 保留较古老的敬拜形式、教义或戒律的运动
senses.example: Religious traditionalism kept the old liturgy in a language few understood.
senses.exampleCN: 宗教传统主义保留了那种少有人懂的古老礼仪语言。
senses.why: Faith is where inherited form feels most like content, so defending the old rite becomes defending the faith itself.
senses.whyCN: 在信仰里，继承的形式最像内容本身，因此捍卫旧礼仪就等于捍卫信仰。

senses.title: Artistic traditionalism
senses.definition: the practice of working within inherited styles, techniques and canons
senses.definitionCN: 在继承的风格、技法与经典规范内创作的做法
senses.example: The academy's traditionalism kept the figure at the centre of painting.
senses.exampleCN: 学院的 traditionalism 让“人像”继续占据绘画的中心。
senses.why: In art the word usually marks the party of the workshop and the academy against the party of experiment.
senses.whyCN: 在艺术里，这个词通常标记画室与学院一派，对立于实验一派。

senses.title: Educational traditionalism
senses.definition: the view that schooling should transmit a canon and tested methods rather than experiment
senses.definitionCN: 认为学校教育应传递经典与经过检验的方法、而非试验新法的观点
senses.example: Educational traditionalism defends memory work and the reading of whole books.
senses.exampleCN: 教育传统主义为背诵与整本书阅读辩护。
senses.why: Schools are the institution most directly responsible for handing on a culture, so the argument about tradition is sharpest there.
senses.whyCN: 学校是最直接负责传递文化的机构，因此关于传统的争论在那里最尖锐。

senses.title: Political traditionalism
senses.definition: a political stance that values inherited institutions, hierarchy and slow reform
senses.definitionCN: 重视继承制度、等级与缓慢改革的政治立场
senses.example: Political traditionalism distrusts constitutions written from scratch.
senses.exampleCN: 政治传统主义不信任从头写起的宪法。
senses.why: The doctrine becomes political when it defends not a song or a rite but a system of offices and obligations.
senses.whyCN: 当它捍卫的不再是一首歌或一场礼仪，而是一套职位与义务的体系，这套学说就变成政治立场。

senses.title: A style or period label
senses.definition: a label used by critics for art or writing that deliberately stays within old forms
senses.definitionCN: 评论家用来指有意停留在旧形式中的艺术或写作的标签
senses.example: The critic called the poet's traditionalism a choice, not a limitation.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家把这位诗人的传统主义称为一种选择，而非局限。
senses.why: Critics need a neutral name for work that is old-fashioned by design, so the doctrine becomes a descriptive label.
senses.whyCN: 评论家需要一个中性名词来指有意守旧的作品，于是这套主张变成描述性标签。

senses.title: Everyday resistance to rapid change
senses.definition: an ordinary person's reluctance to abandon familiar ways when change arrives quickly
senses.definitionCN: 变化来得太快时，普通人不愿放弃熟悉方式的心理
senses.example: The shopkeeper's traditionalism is not a theory; it is a refusal to throw away a working scale.
senses.exampleCN: 这位店主的传统主义不是理论，而是不肯扔掉一台还能用的秤。
senses.why: The grand doctrine has a small cousin: anyone can be called traditionalist for keeping what still works.
senses.whyCN: 宏大的学说有一个小小的亲戚：任何保留仍管用之物的人，都可能被称为传统主义者。

intro.en: Traditionalism joins tradition, from Latin traditio and tradere, with the doctrine suffix -ism, from Greek -ismos through Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: traditionalism 由 tradition 与表示学说的后缀 -ism 结合而成；tradition 来自拉丁语 traditio 与 tradere，-ism 经拉丁语来自希腊语 -ismos。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tradere meant to hand over or deliver, built from trans-, across, and dare, to give. The image is a transfer from one hand to another.
items.cn: tradere 意为「交出、交付」，由表示「越过」的 trans- 与 dare「给」构成。意象是从一只手交到另一只手。

items.en: Traditio named the act of handing over and, by extension, what is handed down as teaching or custom.
items.cn: traditio 指交出这一动作，并引申为作为教导或习俗传下的内容。

items.en: Old French tradition carried the word into English, where it first meant delivery and later inheritance of custom.
items.cn: 古法语 tradition 把这个词带入英语，最初指交付，后来指习俗的继承。

items.en: The suffix -ismos named a practice or doctrine and became Latin -ismus and English -ism, building realism, socialism and traditionalism alike.
items.cn: 后缀 -ismos 指某种实践或学说，后来变成拉丁语 -ismus 与英语 -ism，同样构成 realism（写实主义）、socialism（社会主义）与 traditionalism。

items.en: Traditionalism appeared as a named stance in the nineteenth century, first in religious controversy and then in politics and the arts.
items.cn: traditionalism 在十九世纪成为一种有名目的立场，先出现在宗教争论，随后进入政治与艺术。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of traditionalism is dated differently by different reference works, so the earliest citation should be treated as doubtful.
items.cn: 来源不确定：各家参考资料对 traditionalism 在英语中的最早使用说法不一，因此最早书证应视为存疑。

note.en: The first group holds forms of the same tradition stock; the second holds stances that are often confused with traditionalism.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 tradition 词干的词；第二组是常与传统主义混淆的立场。

entries.definition: A custom or body of customs handed down; traditionalism is the deliberate preference for such customs.
entries.definitionCN: 传下的习俗或习俗总体；traditionalism 是对这类习俗的有意偏好。

entries.definition: Describing something that follows tradition; it does not name a doctrine or a movement.
entries.definitionCN: 描述遵循传统的事物；它不命名一套学说或运动。

entries.definition: A person who supports traditionalism; the -ist form names an adherent, not the stance.
entries.definitionCN: 支持传统主义的人；带 -ist 的形式指拥护者，不指立场。

entries.definition: Marked by traditionalist ideas; it describes the flavour of a work or policy rather than the doctrine itself.
entries.definitionCN: 带传统主义色彩的；它描述作品或政策的味道，而非学说本身。

entries.definition: A preference for existing institutions and slow change; traditionalism is one current within it, often stressing inherited culture.
entries.definitionCN: 偏好既有制度与缓慢变化；传统主义是其中一股，常强调继承文化。

entries.definition: Adherence to officially correct belief; it concerns doctrine, while traditionalism concerns inherited practice.
entries.definitionCN: 遵奉官方正确的信仰；它关心教义，而传统主义关心继承的实践。

entries.definition: Attachment to accepted social conventions; it is about manners and norms, not a defence of tradition as wisdom.
entries.definitionCN: 依附于被接受的社会惯例；它关乎礼俗与规范，而不是把传统当作智慧来捍卫。

entries.definition: A desire to restore an earlier order; traditionalism can be conservative without wanting to reverse history.
entries.definitionCN: 渴望恢复较早秩序；传统主义可以是保守的，却不一定想倒转历史。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real handover root, the doctrine suffix and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「交接」的真实词根、表示学说的后缀，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: tradition plus the doctrine suffix: the same ending builds realism and socialism, so the word names a stance rather than a custom.
normal.cn: tradition 加表示学说的后缀：同一词尾也构成 realism（写实主义）与 socialism（社会主义），因此这个词命名一种立场，而不是一项习俗。

normal.en: The family runs tradition, traditional, traditionalist, traditionalistic, traditionalism and traditionally.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 tradition（传统）、traditional（传统的）、traditionalist（传统主义者）、traditionalistic（带传统主义色彩的）、traditionalism（传统主义）、traditionally（传统上）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: religious traditionalism, political traditionalism, educational traditionalism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：宗教传统主义、政治传统主义、教育传统主义。

normal.en: The core image is a handover: tradition is what is passed, traditionalism is the choice to keep passing it.
normal.cn: 核心意象是交接：传统是被传的东西，传统主义是选择继续传下去。

normal.en: Its usual rival in argument is progressivism, not modernity.
normal.cn: 在争论中，它通常的对手是进步主义，而不是现代性。

abstract.en: Picture a repaired bench that has outlasted three replacements.
abstract.cn: 想象一张修了又修的板凳，比三次更换都活得久。

abstract.en: Picture a hand refusing to open because the thing inside still works.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手不肯松开，因为掌心里的东西仍然管用。

abstract.en: Picture a clock kept wound not because it is right, but because it was your grandfather's.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟一直上着弦，不是因为它准，而是因为它是祖父的。

examples.en: Traditionalism in the village protected the dialect but also kept strangers out.
examples.cn: 村里的传统主义保护了方言，却也把外来者挡在门外。

examples.en: The composer's traditionalism is audible in every unresolved cadence.
examples.cn: 这位作曲家的传统主义在每一个未解决的终止式里都听得见。

examples.en: Traditionalism is not the same as memory; it turns memory into a rule.
examples.cn: 传统主义不等于记忆；它把记忆变成一条规则。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「传」加「统」再加「主义」——把老祖宗传下的规矩当成主张来守，就是传统主义。

root: 由 tradition 加表示学说的后缀 -ism 构成。tradition 来自拉丁语 traditio「交出、传下」，而 traditio 出自动词 tradere「交出」，由 trans-「越过」与 dare「给」构成；-ism 经拉丁语 -ismus 源自希腊语 -ismos。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one preference: inherited ways are kept, then defended as philosophy, faith, art, schooling, politics, a label and finally a shopkeeper's small refusal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种偏好展开：先保留继承的方式，再把它辩护为哲学、信仰、艺术、教育、政治、标签，最后是店主那点小小的不情愿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand passing down an object and another hand refusing to let it go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把物件传下，另一只手不肯放开。

branches.en: PREFERENCE AND HABIT: the same reluctance appears as a doctrine in one person and as a working scale in another.
branches.cn: 偏好与习惯：同一种不情愿，在一个人身上是学说，在另一个人身上是一台还能用的秤。

branches.en: PHILOSOPHY AND POLITICS: age becomes an argument, and the argument becomes a defence of institutions.
branches.cn: 哲学与政治：年岁变成论据，论据又变成对制度的辩护。

branches.en: FAITH: inherited rite feels like the content of belief itself.
branches.cn: 信仰：继承的礼仪感觉像信仰内容本身。

branches.en: ART AND LABEL: the academy's style is later named by critics as a period choice.
branches.cn: 艺术与标签：学院的风格后来被评论家命名为一种时期选择。

branches.en: SCHOOLING: the institution that hands on culture argues most sharply about what to hand on.
branches.cn: 学校教育：负责传递文化的机构，对「传什么」争论得最尖锐。

intro.en: Traditionalism is a handover noun, an adjective ending and a doctrine suffix, all still readable in the word.
intro.cn: traditionalism 是一个表示交接的名词、一个形容词词尾与一个表示学说的后缀，三者在词里仍可读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin trans- and dare build tradere, traditio supplies the noun, -alis the adjective, and -ismus the doctrine.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trans- 与 dare 构成 tradere，traditio 提供名词，-alis 提供形容词，-ismus 提供学说名词。

items.example: The prefix also builds transfer and transport.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀也构成 transfer（转移）与 transport（运输）。

items.example: The verb also builds data, things given.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也构成 data，即「被给出之物」。

items.example: The verb gave tradition and traitor alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时给出 tradition（传统）与 traitor（叛徒）。

items.example: The noun became English tradition through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词经法语成为英语 tradition。

items.example: The ending builds traditional and natural.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 traditional（传统的）与 natural（自然的）。

items.example: The ending builds realism and socialism.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 realism（写实主义）与 socialism（社会主义）。

items.example: Religious traditionalism kept the old rite.
items.exampleCN: 宗教传统主义保留了旧礼仪。

items.example: The traditionalist refused the new calendar.
items.exampleCN: 这位传统主义者拒绝新历法。

items.example: The design is traditionalistic.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计带传统主义色彩。

latinEntries.structure: tradere, tradidi, traditum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
latinEntries.meaning: to hand over; to deliver; to betray

definition_zh: 现代化；使社会、经济、制度或设备变得现代的过程；现代化理论；技术更新
definition_en: the process of making a society, economy, institution or equipment modern
core_image: 老厂房里，工人把最后一台手摇车床推出去，换上带屏幕的新机器
scene: 老厂房里，工人把最后一台手摇车床推出去，换上带屏幕的新机器，The factory's modernization replaced hand tools with computer-controlled machines.
sceneCN: 这里 modernization 指「设备与生产的技术更新」（第 3 个义项：技术层面的现代化）；句意为这家工厂的现代化用电脑控制的机器取代了手工工具。图中可辨识物件：手摇车床、带屏幕的新机器、搬运轨道、工人的手套。

pos.zh: 现代化；现代化的过程；技术更新

senses.title: The process of becoming modern
senses.definition: the broad process by which a society acquires modern industry, institutions and ways of life
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会获得现代工业、制度与生活方式的总过程
senses.example: Modernization changed the valley within one generation.
senses.exampleCN: 现代化在一代人的时间里改变了这座山谷。
senses.why: The suffix names a process rather than a state: the word looks at the movement toward modernity, not at modernity itself.
senses.whyCN: 后缀命名的是过程而不是状态：这个词看的是走向现代性的运动，而非现代性本身。

senses.title: The sociological paradigm
senses.definition: the body of theory that explains development as a series of stages from traditional to modern society
senses.definitionCN: 把发展解释为从传统社会到现代社会一系列阶段的理论总体
senses.example: Modernization was the dominant framework in development studies after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 战后，现代化曾是发展研究中的主导框架。
senses.why: A process this large needs a theory, so the same noun names the academic paradigm that tried to describe it.
senses.whyCN: 如此庞大的过程需要理论，因此同一个名词也命名试图描述它的学术范式。

senses.title: Technical upgrading of equipment
senses.definition: the replacement of old machinery, systems or methods with newer and more efficient ones
senses.definitionCN: 用更新、更高效的机器、系统或方法替换旧的
senses.example: The factory's modernization replaced hand tools with computer-controlled machines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂的现代化用电脑控制的机器取代了手工工具。
senses.why: The grand process has a workshop-sized version: one machine at a time, the old is pushed out and the new is wired in.
senses.whyCN: 宏大的过程有一个车间大小的版本：一次换一台机器，旧的被推出去，新的被接上电线。

senses.title: Urban and infrastructural development
senses.definition: the building of roads, housing, water and power systems to modern standards
senses.definitionCN: 按现代标准建设道路、住房、供水与电力系统
senses.example: Modernization brought the first paved road to the fishing village.
senses.exampleCN: 现代化把第一条铺装路带到了这个渔村。
senses.why: Modern life has a physical shell, and the noun often names the laying of that shell: pipes, wires, asphalt.
senses.whyCN: 现代生活有一层物质外壳，这个名词常指铺这层外壳：管道、电线、沥青。

senses.title: Economic and industrial development
senses.definition: the shift from farming and small craft to industry, wage labour and higher output
senses.definitionCN: 从农业与手工副业转向工业、雇佣劳动与更高产量
senses.example: Economic modernization moved workers from the fields to the mills.
senses.exampleCN: 经济现代化把工人从田里移到了工厂。
senses.why: Economists use the word for the measurable part of the change: where people work and what they produce.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家用这个词指变化中可测量的部分：人在哪里工作、生产什么。

senses.title: Institutional and legal reform
senses.definition: the reform of government, law and administration along modern lines
senses.definitionCN: 按现代方式改革政府、法律与行政
senses.example: Legal modernization removed the old courts and created a written code.
senses.exampleCN: 法律现代化废除了旧法庭，制定了一部成文法典。
senses.why: Industry needs contracts and records, so the process reaches into courts, registries and tax offices.
senses.whyCN: 工业需要合同与记录，因此这一过程延伸到法院、登记处与税务所。

senses.title: Cultural change toward modern values
senses.definition: the spread of values such as mobility, individual choice, science and secular time
senses.definitionCN: 流动性、个人选择、科学与世俗时间观等价值的传播
senses.example: Modernization altered how families arranged marriages and kept time.
senses.exampleCN: 现代化改变了家庭安排婚姻与计算时间的方式。
senses.why: The process is not only machines: it changes what people expect from life and from each other.
senses.whyCN: 这个过程不只是机器：它改变人们对生活、对彼此的期待。

senses.title: The state of being modernized
senses.definition: the result of the process, viewed as a completed condition
senses.definitionCN: 过程的结果，被视为已完成的状态
senses.example: The port's modernization is visible in its cranes and its silence.
senses.exampleCN: 这座港口的现代化在吊车与寂静中都看得见。
senses.why: A process noun can be read backwards as a result: what has been modernized is now a condition.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词也可以倒过来读成结果：已经被现代化的东西，如今成了一种状态。

intro.en: Modernization is modern plus the verb ending -ize and the process ending -ation, ultimately from Late Latin modernus and modo. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: modernization 由 modern 加动词词尾 -ize 与过程词尾 -ation 构成，最终来自晚期拉丁语 modernus 与 modo。年代均为约数。

items.en: Modo meant just now. It is usually derived from modus, measure or manner, though that link is a standard account rather than a recorded certainty.
items.cn: modo 意为「刚刚」。通行说法认为它来自 modus「尺度、方式」，但这一联系只是标准解释，并非有记录的确证。

items.en: Late Latin modernus, of the present time, was built from the time word plus -nus.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 modernus 意为「当下的」，由这个时间词加 -nus 构成。

items.en: The verb ending -ize came through Latin -izare from Greek -izein, meaning to make, practise or become.
items.cn: 动词词尾 -ize 经拉丁语 -izare 来自希腊语 -izein，意为「使、从事或成为」。

items.en: The noun ending -ation came from Latin -atio, which named an action or its result.
items.cn: 名词词尾 -ation 来自拉丁语 -atio，表示动作或其结果。

items.en: Modernization appeared in the nineteenth century as industry and administration began to be described as a single process.
items.cn: modernization 在十九世纪出现，当时工业与行政开始被描述为同一个过程。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of modernization is not securely dated, and the pre-Latin origin of modo and modus is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：modernization 在英语中的最早使用没有确切年代；modo 与 modus 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds members of the same modern- family; the second holds processes that are often mistaken for modernization itself.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 modern- 词族的成员；第二组是常被误当作现代化本身的过程。

entries.definition: To make something modern; modernization is the process noun built from that verb.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物现代化；modernization 是由该动词构成的过程名词。

entries.definition: Belonging to the present age; it describes a thing, while modernization describes the change that made it so.
entries.definitionCN: 属于当下时代的；它描述事物，而 modernization 描述使之如此的变化。

entries.definition: The state of being modern; modernization is the road, modernity is the place arrived at.
entries.definitionCN: 现代的状态；modernization 是道路，modernity 是抵达的地方。

entries.definition: The artistic and intellectual movement that broke with inherited forms; it is cultural, while modernization is social and technical.
entries.definitionCN: 打破继承形式的艺术与思想运动；它属于文化，而 modernization 属于社会与技术。

entries.definition: Improvement in economic and social conditions; modernization is one model of how development should happen.
entries.definitionCN: 经济与社会状况的改善；现代化是关于发展应如何发生的一种模型。

entries.definition: The growth of manufacturing industry; it is one part of modernization, not the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 制造业的增长；它是现代化的一部分，而非全过程。

entries.definition: Adoption of Western institutions and culture; critics use it to say that modernization was never neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 采纳西方的制度与文化；批评者用它指出现代化从来不是中立的。

entries.definition: An improvement to one machine or system; modernization suggests a broader and longer process.
entries.definitionCN: 对单台机器或系统的改进；modernization 暗示更广、更长的过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real modern stem, the real process endings and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 modern 词干、真实的过程词尾，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: modern plus the make-verb ending and the process ending: the word is literally the making of the modern.
normal.cn: modern 加表示「使……」的动词词尾与表示过程的名词词尾：这个词字面上就是「使现代的过程」。

normal.en: The family runs modern, modernize, modernization, modernity, modernism and modernizer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 modern（现代的）、modernize（使现代化）、modernization（现代化）、modernity（现代性）、modernism（现代主义）、modernizer（推动现代化的人）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: economic modernization, industrial modernization, technical modernization.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：经济现代化、工业现代化、技术现代化。

normal.en: The word is a road, not a destination: modernity is where the road arrives.
normal.cn: 这个词是一条路，不是终点：modernity 才是路抵达的地方。

normal.en: Its common critique is that it treats one model of development as universal.
normal.cn: 对它的常见批评是：它把一种发展模型当作普遍标准。

abstract.en: Picture an old lathe rolled out of a factory while a new machine is wired in.
abstract.cn: 想象一台旧车床被推出厂房，同时一台新机器正在接线。

abstract.en: Picture a village where the first paved road arrives before the first streetlight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个村庄，第一条铺装路先于第一盏路灯到来。

abstract.en: Picture a clock changing from church bells to factory whistles.
abstract.cn: 想象计时方式从教堂钟声变成工厂汽笛。

examples.en: Modernization promised wealth and delivered a new kind of dependence.
examples.cn: 现代化许诺财富，却交出一种新的依赖。

examples.en: The archive's modernization put every ledger online.
examples.cn: 档案馆的现代化把每一本账册都搬上了网。

examples.en: Social modernization changed the wedding more than the factory.
examples.cn: 社会现代化对婚礼的改变，胜过对工厂的改变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩登」加「化」——把旧东西一步步变成摩登的样子，就是现代化。

root: 由 modern 加动词词尾 -ize 与过程词尾 -ation 构成。modern 来自晚期拉丁语 modernus「当下的」，通行说法追溯至 modo「刚刚」，modo 又常被解释为来自 modus「尺度、方式」；-ize 经拉丁语 -izare 源自希腊语 -izein，-ation 来自拉丁语 -atio。modo 与 modus 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process: a society, a theory, a machine, a road, an economy, a court, a value and finally the finished state.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个过程展开：一个社会、一套理论、一台机器、一条路、一个经济、一座法院、一种价值，最后是完成后的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old machine rolled out while a new one is wired in.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧机器被推出，新机器正在接线。

branches.en: PROCESS AND RESULT: the same word can look forward to the change or backward at what has been changed.
branches.cn: 过程与结果：同一个词既可以向前看变化，也可以回头看在变化之后的状态。

branches.en: THEORY: the process becomes a paradigm that claims to explain all societies.
branches.cn: 理论：这个过程变成一套声称能解释所有社会的范式。

branches.en: MACHINE: the workshop-sized version, one lathe at a time.
branches.cn: 机器：车间大小的版本，一次换一台车床。

branches.en: ROAD AND ECONOMY: pipes, asphalt and wages make the new life possible.
branches.cn: 道路与经济：管道、沥青与工资使新生活成为可能。

branches.en: LAW AND VALUES: courts need written codes, and families need new expectations.
branches.cn: 法律与价值：法院需要成文法典，家庭需要新的期待。

intro.en: Modernization stacks a time adjective, a make-verb ending and a process noun ending.
intro.cn: modernization 叠了一个时间形容词、一个表示「使……」的动词词尾与一个过程名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin modo and modernus supply the adjective, Greek -izein through Latin supplies the verb, and Latin -atio supplies the process noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modo 与 modernus 提供形容词，希腊语 -izein 经拉丁语提供动词，拉丁语 -atio 提供过程名词。

items.example: The adverb is usually linked to modus, measure.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词通常被联系到 modus「尺度」。

items.example: The adjective entered English through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词经法语进入英语。

items.example: The ending builds modernize and industrialize.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 modernize（使现代化）与 industrialize（使工业化）。

items.example: The ending builds modernization and industrialization.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 modernization（现代化）与 industrialization（工业化）。

items.example: The mill modernized its looms.
items.exampleCN: 磨坊把织机现代化了。

items.example: Modernization changed the harbour.
items.exampleCN: 现代化改变了这座港口。

items.example: The modernizer rebuilt the telegraph line.
items.exampleCN: 这位现代化推动者重建了电报线。

items.example: Modernity arrived before modernization was complete.
items.exampleCN: 现代性在现代化完成之前就到来了。

items.meaning: the cultural movement of the new
items.example: Modernism changed the gallery, not the factory.
items.exampleCN: 现代主义改变的是画廊，不是工厂。

definition_zh: 使现代化；更新设备与技术；改革制度；使（语言、拼写、建筑）现代化；现代化（不及物，少用）
definition_en: to make something modern in style, equipment, method or organization
core_image: 磨坊的旧皮带轮已经磨得发滑，账本上的维修费一年比一年高
scene: 磨坊的皮带轮已经磨得发滑，账本上的维修费一年比一年高，The old mill must modernize its equipment or close.
sceneCN: 这里 modernize 指「更新设备与技术」（第 2 个义项：技术设备更新）；句意为这座老磨坊必须更新设备，否则就得关门。图中可辨识物件：磨滑的皮带轮、维修账本、待换的新齿轮、关门的木牌。

pos.zh: 使现代化；更新设备；改革制度；使现代化（不及物，少用）

senses.title: Make modern in style or design
senses.titleCN: 在风格或设计上使现代化
senses.definition: to change the appearance or design of something so that it looks contemporary
senses.definitionCN: 改变某物的外观或设计，使其看起来属于当代
senses.example: They modernized the lobby with glass and steel.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用玻璃与钢材使大堂现代化。
senses.why: The verb starts with the visible: what looks old is made to look new.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词从可见处开始：看起来旧的东西被弄得看起来新。

senses.title: Update equipment and technology
senses.definition: to replace old machines or systems with newer and more efficient ones
senses.definitionCN: 用更新、更高效的机器或系统替换旧的
senses.example: The old mill must modernize its equipment or close.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老磨坊必须更新设备，否则就得关门。
senses.why: Here the verb has a hard test: if the old machine still turns, it can wait; if it slips, modernization becomes urgent.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词有一道硬检验：旧机器还能转就还能等；一旦打滑，现代化就变得紧迫。

senses.title: Reform institutions and laws
senses.definition: to bring government, law or administration into a modern form
senses.definitionCN: 使政府、法律或行政进入现代形式
senses.example: The new state modernized its courts before it built its railways.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新国家先改革了法院，再修铁路。
senses.why: The verb can act on abstractions: a code, a ministry or a tax system can be brought up to date.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以对抽象物起作用：一部法典、一个部门或一套税制都可以被更新。

senses.title: Bring a society to modern industry
senses.definition: to transform an economy or society by introducing industry, wage labour and modern infrastructure
senses.definitionCN: 通过引入工业、雇佣劳动与现代基础设施来改造经济或社会
senses.example: The plan aimed to modernize the whole province within twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划打算在二十年内使全省现代化。
senses.why: The verb can take a whole society as its object, and then it means the entire package of industry, cities and administration.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以拿整个社会作宾语，此时它指工业、城市与行政的整套组合。

senses.title: Modernize language or spelling
senses.definition: to change spelling, vocabulary or usage to match current practice
senses.definitionCN: 改变拼写、词汇或用法，以符合当前惯例
senses.example: The editors modernized the spelling but kept the punctuation.
senses.exampleCN: 编者把拼写现代化了，却保留了原来的标点。
senses.why: Language is inherited too, so the same verb can be applied to orthography: old letters are replaced by current ones.
senses.whyCN: 语言也是继承来的，因此同一个动词可以用在正字法上：旧字母被当下的字母替换。

senses.title: Renovate a building or facility
senses.definition: to repair and update a building so that it meets current standards
senses.definitionCN: 修缮并更新一栋建筑，使其符合当前标准
senses.example: The library was modernized without losing its reading room.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆被现代化了，却没有丢掉它的阅览室。
senses.why: A building can be modernized inside while its shell stays old, which shows that the verb changes systems rather than age.
senses.whyCN: 一栋建筑可以内部现代化、外壳仍旧，这说明动词改的是系统，而不是年岁。

senses.title: Adopt modern methods
senses.definition: to switch to current techniques in farming, industry or administration
senses.definitionCN: 在农业、工业或行政中改用当前技术
senses.example: The cooperative modernized its irrigation and doubled the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 合作社使灌溉现代化，收成翻了一倍。
senses.why: The object can be a method rather than a thing: what is modernized is the way work is done.
senses.whyCN: 宾语可以是方法而非物件：被现代化的是做事的方式。

senses.title: Become modern (intransitive, rare)
senses.definition: to become modern without an explicit object, used mainly in older or technical writing
senses.definitionCN: 不带明确宾语地变得现代，主要用于较早或专业写作
senses.example: The town modernized slowly, one street at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇慢慢地现代化，一次一条街。
senses.why: Most uses are transitive, but the verb can stand alone when the subject is the thing changing itself.
senses.whyCN: 多数用法是及物的，但当主语就是自行变化之物时，这个动词也可以单独使用。

intro.en: Modernize is modern plus the verb ending -ize, which reached English through Latin from Greek -izein. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: modernize 是 modern 加动词词尾 -ize 构成，后者经拉丁语从希腊语 -izein 进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Modo meant just now; it is usually derived from modus, measure or manner, though that link is a standard account rather than a certainty.
items.cn: modo 意为「刚刚」；通行说法认为它来自 modus「尺度、方式」，但这一联系只是标准解释，并非确证。

items.en: Late Latin modernus, of the present time, was built from the time word plus -nus and reached English through French.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 modernus 意为「当下的」，由这个时间词加 -nus 构成，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: The ending -ize came through Latin -izare from Greek -izein, meaning to make, practise or become.
items.cn: 词尾 -ize 经拉丁语 -izare 来自希腊语 -izein，意为「使、从事或成为」。

items.en: French moderniser appeared in the eighteenth century, and English modernize followed the same pattern.
items.cn: 法语 moderniser 在十八世纪出现，英语 modernize 沿用了同一构词方式。

items.en: English modernize first meant to give a modern form to language or design, and later extended to industry and institutions.
items.cn: 英语 modernize 最初指给语言或设计以现代形式，后来扩展到工业与制度。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of modernize is not securely dated, and the pre-Latin origin of modo and modus remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：modernize 在英语中的最早使用没有确切年代；modo 与 modus 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds members of the same modern- family; the second holds verbs of improvement that are often used in its place.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 modern- 词族的成员；第二组是常被用来替代它的「改进」类动词。

entries.definition: The process of making modern; modernize is the verb that names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 使现代化的过程；modernize 是命名该动作的动词。

entries.definition: Belonging to the present age; the adjective describes the result, while the verb describes the act of producing it.
entries.definitionCN: 属于当下时代的；形容词描述结果，动词描述产生结果的动作。

entries.definition: The state of being modern; the verb cannot be replaced by this noun without losing the action.
entries.definitionCN: 现代的状态；这个名词不能替代动词，否则动作就丢了。

entries.definition: The cultural movement that broke with inherited forms; it is a programme, not an act of upgrading.
entries.definitionCN: 打破继承形式的文化运动；它是一套纲领，不是升级动作。

entries.definition: To add the latest information or changes; narrower than modernize, which can mean a whole social process.
entries.definitionCN: 加入最新信息或改动；比 modernize 窄，后者可指整个社会过程。

entries.definition: To replace something with a better version; it usually applies to one item, while modernize can apply to a system.
entries.definitionCN: 用更好的版本替换；通常用于单件物品，而 modernize 可用于整个系统。

entries.definition: To restore a building to good condition; it may keep the old style, while modernize changes the style or system.
entries.definitionCN: 把建筑修复到良好状态；它可能保留旧风格，而 modernize 会改变风格或系统。

entries.definition: To change an institution for the better; it stresses improvement, while modernize stresses becoming current.
entries.definitionCN: 为改善而改变制度；它强调改善，而 modernize 强调变得合乎当下。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real modern stem, the real make-verb ending and the phrases the verb actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 modern 词干、表示「使……」的真实动词词尾，以及这个动词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: modern plus the make-verb ending: the word means to make modern, as activate means to make active.
normal.cn: modern 加表示「使……」的动词词尾：这个词意为「使现代」，就像 activate 意为「使活动」。

normal.en: The family runs modern, modernize, modernization, modernizer, modernity and modernism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 modern（现代的）、modernize（使现代化）、modernization（现代化）、modernizer（推动现代化的人）、modernity（现代性）、modernism（现代主义）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: modernize equipment, modernize the economy, modernize spelling.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：更新设备、使经济现代化、使拼写现代化。

normal.en: The verb is transitive most of the time: someone modernizes something.
normal.cn: 这个动词多数时候是及物的：某人使某物现代化。

normal.en: A useful contrast: renovate repairs, upgrade improves one item, modernize brings a whole system up to date.
normal.cn: 有用的对照：renovate 是修复，upgrade 是改进单件，modernize 是把整套系统更新到当下。

abstract.en: Picture a worn belt being cut and a new one fitted while the wheels keep turning.
abstract.cn: 想象一条磨坏的皮带被剪下，新皮带装上，而轮子还在转。

abstract.en: Picture an old courtroom with new record books and the same wooden bench.
abstract.cn: 想象一间旧法庭，换了新记录册，木凳还是原来那张。

abstract.en: Picture a page of old spelling with every long s crossed out.
abstract.cn: 想象一页旧拼写，每个长 s 都被划掉。

examples.en: The city modernized its water system before the old pipes burst.
examples.cn: 这座城市在旧管道爆裂之前更新了供水系统。

examples.en: She modernized the workshop without firing a single carpenter.
examples.cn: 她把作坊现代化了，却没有辞退一名木匠。

examples.en: The publisher modernized the text but refused to modernize its jokes.
examples.cn: 出版社把文本现代化了，却拒绝改动其中的笑话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩登」加「使……」——把旧东西弄成摩登样子，就是使现代化。

root: 由 modern 加动词词尾 -ize 构成。modern 来自晚期拉丁语 modernus「当下的」，通行说法追溯至 modo「刚刚」，modo 又常被解释为来自 modus「尺度、方式」；-ize 经拉丁语 -izare 源自希腊语 -izein「使、成为」。modo 与 modus 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of making current: a look, a machine, a court, a society, a spelling, a building, a method and finally a town changing itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「使合乎当下」的动作展开：外观、机器、法院、社会、拼写、建筑、方法，最后是一座自行变化的小镇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn belt replaced while the wheels keep turning.
core.cn: 核心意象：磨坏的皮带被替换，而轮子仍在转。

branches.en: SURFACE AND SHELL: a lobby and a library can be made current without changing what they are.
branches.cn: 表面与外壳：大堂与图书馆都可以被更新，而不改变它们是什么。

branches.en: MACHINE AND METHOD: equipment and technique are two ways of doing work differently.
branches.cn: 机器与方法：设备与技术是改变做事方式的两条路。

branches.en: LAW: courts and codes are brought up to date before the railways arrive.
branches.cn: 法律：法院与法典在铁路到来之前就先更新。

branches.en: SOCIETY: the verb can take a whole province as its object.
branches.cn: 社会：这个动词可以拿整个省作宾语。

branches.en: LANGUAGE AND SELF-CHANGE: spelling can be modernized, and a town can modernize itself.
branches.cn: 语言与自行变化：拼写可以被现代化，一座小镇也可以自行现代化。

intro.en: Modernize is a time adjective plus a make-verb ending, and the inflections are perfectly regular.
intro.cn: modernize 是一个时间形容词加一个表示「使……」的动词词尾，其屈折变化完全规则。

latinIntro.en: Latin modo and modernus supply modern, and Greek -izein through Latin -izare supplies the verb ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modo 与 modernus 提供 modern，希腊语 -izein 经拉丁语 -izare 提供动词词尾。

items.example: The adverb is usually linked to modus, measure.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词通常被联系到 modus「尺度」。

items.example: The adjective entered English through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词经法语进入英语。

items.example: The ending builds modernize and organize.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 modernize（使现代化）与 organize（组织）。

items.example: The mill modernized its equipment.
items.exampleCN: 磨坊更新了设备。

items.example: She modernizes old houses.
items.exampleCN: 她翻新老房子。

items.example: The harbour was modernized last year.
items.exampleCN: 这座港口去年完成了现代化。

items.meaning: in the act of making modern
items.example: The modernizing committee met weekly.
items.exampleCN: 现代化委员会每周开会。

items.example: Modernization took a decade.
items.exampleCN: 现代化花了十年。

items.example: The modernizer ordered new looms.
items.exampleCN: 这位现代化推动者订购了新织机。

definition_zh: 现代性；现代的状态；现代社会与文化的处境；现代时期；现代风格
definition_en: the condition, experience or period of being modern
core_image: 深夜的地铁站里广告屏亮着，乘客各自盯着手机，谁也不看谁
scene: 深夜的地铁站里广告屏亮着，乘客各自盯着手机，谁也不看谁，The novel captures the loneliness of modernity in a crowded city.
sceneCN: 这里 modernity 指「现代都市生活的体验与处境」（第 4 个义项：现代生活的文化体验）；句意为这部小说捕捉了拥挤城市中现代性的孤独。图中可辨识物件：广告屏、手机、站台长椅、互不相视的乘客。

pos.zh: 现代性；现代的状态、处境或时期

derivatives.zh: 现代主义者；现代主义的

senses.title: The condition of being modern
senses.definition: the state or quality of belonging to the modern age
senses.definitionCN: 属于现代时代的处境或性质
senses.example: Modernity is not a date but a condition that keeps changing.
senses.exampleCN: 现代性不是一个日期，而是一种不断变化的处境。
senses.why: The suffix names a quality of a thing, so modernity is modern-ness itself, abstracted from any particular object.
senses.whyCN: 后缀命名事物的性质，因此现代性就是「现代」本身，从任何具体物件中抽象出来。

senses.title: A historical period
senses.definition: the era after the medieval period, or the period of modern societies, depending on the field
senses.definitionCN: 中世纪之后的时代，或现代社会所处的时期，视学科而定
senses.example: Historians place the start of modernity at different centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家把现代性的起点放在不同的世纪。
senses.why: A quality can be turned into a period: if societies are modern, there must be a time when modernity begins.
senses.whyCN: 性质可以变成一个时期：如果社会是现代的了，就必然有一个现代性开始的时刻。

senses.title: The sociological condition
senses.definition: the social condition marked by rationalization, secularization, industry and impersonal institutions
senses.definitionCN: 以理性化、世俗化、工业与非人格化制度为特征的社会处境
senses.example: Modernity promised that reason would make institutions predictable.
senses.exampleCN: 现代性曾许诺，理性能让制度变得可预测。
senses.why: Sociology made the abstract quality into a system: modernity is a way of organizing work, belief and time.
senses.whyCN: 社会学把这个抽象性质变成一个系统：现代性是组织工作、信仰与时间的一套方式。

senses.title: The experience of modern life
senses.definition: the lived texture of modern life, often described as speed, anonymity and loneliness
senses.definitionCN: 现代生活的实际质感，常被描述为速度、匿名与孤独
senses.example: The novel captures the loneliness of modernity in a crowded city.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说捕捉了拥挤城市中现代性的孤独。
senses.why: The same condition can be felt rather than measured: crowds, screens and speed produce a new inner weather.
senses.whyCN: 同一种处境可以被感受，而不只是被测量：人群、屏幕与速度造出一种新的内心气候。

senses.title: The quality of modern art
senses.definition: the stylistic quality of art that belongs to the modern movement or period
senses.definitionCN: 属于现代运动或时期的艺术风格特质
senses.example: Critics praised the modernity of the score, not its difficulty.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞这部配乐的现代性，而不是它的难度。
senses.why: A work can have modernity as a property, which is how the abstract noun becomes an art-critical judgement.
senses.whyCN: 一件作品可以把现代性作为一种属性，抽象名词由此变成艺术评论的判断。

senses.title: Political modernity
senses.definition: the political condition of constitutional government, citizenship and public law
senses.definitionCN: 宪政、公民身份与公法所构成的政治处境
senses.example: Political modernity made the citizen a bearer of rights rather than a subject.
senses.exampleCN: 政治现代性使公民成为权利持有者，而不再是臣民。
senses.why: Modernity has separate faces, and politics is one: the state is reorganized around law and citizenship.
senses.whyCN: 现代性有各自的面孔，政治是其中之一：国家围绕法律与公民身份被重新组织。

senses.title: Economic modernity
senses.definition: the economic condition of industrial capitalism, mass production and wage labour
senses.definitionCN: 工业资本主义、大规模生产与雇佣劳动所构成的经济处境
senses.example: Economic modernity arrived with the factory clock.
senses.exampleCN: 经济现代性随工厂的时钟一同到来。
senses.why: The same condition can be counted in output and hours, which is how the noun enters economic history.
senses.whyCN: 同一种处境可以用产量与工时来计数，这个名词由此进入经济史。

senses.title: Being up to date in everyday life
senses.titleCN: 日常生活中「跟得上时代」
senses.definition: the ordinary quality of being current, fashionable or technologically up to date
senses.definitionCN: 在当下、时髦或技术上跟得上时代的普通性质
senses.example: The shop's modernity is a card reader and a very old chair.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店的现代性是一台读卡器和一把很旧的椅子。
senses.why: The grand noun has a small everyday version: anyone can have a little modernity, measured in gadgets and habits.
senses.whyCN: 宏大的名词有一个小小的日常版本：任何人都可以拥有一点现代性，用器物与习惯来衡量。

intro.en: Modernity is modern plus the Latin noun ending -ity, which came from -itas. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: modernity 是 modern 加拉丁语名词词尾 -ity 构成，后者来自 -itas。年代均为约数。

items.en: Modo meant just now; it is usually derived from modus, measure or manner, though that link is a standard account rather than a certainty.
items.cn: modo 意为「刚刚」；通行说法认为它来自 modus「尺度、方式」，但这一联系只是标准解释，并非确证。

items.en: Late Latin modernus, of the present time, was built from the time word plus -nus; English modern came through French.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 modernus 意为「当下的」，由这个时间词加 -nus 构成；英语 modern 经法语进入。

items.en: The noun ending -itas named a state or quality, as in civitas from civis. English -ity continues it.
items.cn: 名词词尾 -itas 命名状态或性质，如 civitas 来自 civis。英语的 -ity 延续了它。

items.en: French modernité appeared in the nineteenth century, and English modernity followed in the same period.
items.cn: 法语 modernité 在十九世纪出现，英语 modernity 也在同一时期跟进。

items.en: Sociologists made modernity a technical term for the condition of industrial, rationalized societies, distinct from modernization as a process.
items.cn: 社会学家把 modernity 变成指工业、理性化社会处境的技术术语，并与作为过程的 modernization 区分开。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of modernity is dated differently, and the pre-Latin origin of modo and modus remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：modernity 在英语中的最早使用各家记载不一；modo 与 modus 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds members of the same modern- family that are often swapped; the second holds terms for the modern age or its mood.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 modern- 词族、常被误换的词；第二组是关于现代时代或其情绪的词。

entries.definition: The artistic movement that broke with inherited forms; modernity is the condition that the movement responded to.
entries.definitionCN: 打破继承形式的艺术运动；modernity 是该运动所回应的处境。

entries.definition: The process of becoming modern; modernity is the state reached, or the experience of living in it.
entries.definitionCN: 走向现代的过程；modernity 是抵达的状态，或身处其中的体验。

entries.definition: Belonging to the present age; the adjective qualifies a thing, while modernity names the condition itself.
entries.definitionCN: 属于当下时代的；形容词修饰事物，而 modernity 命名处境本身。

entries.definition: A way or manner of doing something; it shares a distant Latin root with modern but means a method, not an era.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的方式；它与 modern 共享遥远的拉丁词根，但指方法，不指时代。

entries.definition: The quality of existing at the same time; it stresses the shared present, while modernity stresses a historical condition.
entries.definitionCN: 同时存在的性质；它强调共处的当下，而 modernity 强调历史处境。

entries.definition: The eighteenth century movement that trusted reason and progress; it is one source of modernity, not modernity itself.
entries.definitionCN: 十八世纪信任理性与进步的运动；它是现代性的一个来源，而非现代性本身。

entries.definition: Advance toward a better condition; modernity may believe in progress, but the noun does not itself mean improvement.
entries.definitionCN: 朝更好处境的推进；现代性可能相信进步，但这个名词本身不表示改善。

entries.definition: The growth of cities; it is a major producer of modern experience, not a synonym for modernity.
entries.definitionCN: 城市的增长；它是现代体验的主要制造者，而不是现代性的同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real quality ending, the real modern stem and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示性质的真实词尾、真实的 modern 词干，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: modern plus the quality ending -ity: the same ending builds reality and activity, so modernity is the state of being modern.
normal.cn: modern 加表示性质的名词词尾 -ity：同一词尾也构成 reality（真实）与 activity（活动），所以 modernity 就是「现代的状态」。

normal.en: The family runs modern, modernity, modernization, modernism, modernist and modernize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 modern（现代的）、modernity（现代性）、modernization（现代化）、modernism（现代主义）、modernist（现代主义者）、modernize（使现代化）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: late modernity, early modernity, urban modernity, political modernity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：晚期现代性、早期现代性、城市现代性、政治现代性。

normal.en: The word is a condition, not a process: modernization is the road, modernity is where you stand.
normal.cn: 这个词是处境，不是过程：modernization 是路，modernity 是你站立的地方。

normal.en: Its art-world cousin is modernism, which is a movement rather than a condition.
normal.cn: 它在艺术界的亲戚是 modernism（现代主义），后者是运动，而不是处境。

abstract.en: Picture a crowded platform where every face is lit from below by a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一个拥挤的站台，每张脸都被屏幕从下方照亮。

abstract.en: Picture a clock tower replaced by a timetable that never sleeps.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟楼被一张从不休息的时刻表取代。

abstract.en: Picture a room with the newest reader and the oldest chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，有最新的读卡器和最旧的椅子。

examples.en: Modernity is uneven: the same city can be early modern and late modern in one street.
examples.cn: 现代性并不均衡：同一座城市可以在一条街上同时是早期现代与晚期现代。

examples.en: The painter's modernity lies in what she leaves out.
examples.cn: 这位画家的现代性在于她省略了什么。

examples.en: Critics of modernity ask whether rational order has made life colder.
examples.cn: 现代性的批评者追问：理性秩序是否让生活更冷了？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩登」加「性」——一个时代整体的摩登状态与体验，就是现代性。

root: 由 modern 加表示性质的名词词尾 -ity 构成，-ity 来自拉丁语 -itas。modern 来自晚期拉丁语 modernus「当下的」，通行说法追溯至 modo「刚刚」，modo 又常被解释为来自 modus「尺度、方式」。modo 与 modus 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one condition: a quality, a period, a social system, a felt experience, an artistic property, a politics, an economy and a small everyday version.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种处境展开：一种性质、一个时期、一套社会系统、一种切身感受、一种艺术属性、一种政治、一种经济，最后是一个小小的日常版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowded platform lit by screens, where everyone is modern and alone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个被屏幕照亮的拥挤站台，人人都是现代的，也人人孤独。

branches.en: QUALITY AND HABIT: modernity can be a grand condition or a card reader in a small shop.
branches.cn: 性质与习惯：现代性可以是宏大的处境，也可以是一家小店里的读卡器。

branches.en: PERIOD: a quality becomes a dateable era with a beginning and an end.
branches.cn: 时期：一种性质变成有起点与终点的可断代时代。

branches.en: SYSTEM: rationalization, secularization and industry organize life impersonally.
branches.cn: 系统：理性化、世俗化与工业以非人格的方式组织生活。

branches.en: EXPERIENCE: the system is felt as speed, anonymity and loneliness.
branches.cn: 体验：这套系统被感受为速度、匿名与孤独。

branches.en: FACES: art, politics and economy each show a distinct face of the same condition.
branches.cn: 面孔：艺术、政治与经济各自显出同一处境的不同面孔。

intro.en: Modernity is a time adjective plus the Latin quality ending, and the same stem builds the process and the movement words.
intro.cn: modernity 是一个时间形容词加拉丁语性质词尾，同一词干又造出过程词与运动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin modernus supplies modern, and -itas supplies the noun of quality that became English -ity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modernus 提供 modern，-itas 提供后来成为英语 -ity 的性质名词词尾。

items.exampleCN: 这个副词通常被联系到 modus「尺度」。

items.example: The adjective entered English through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词经法语进入英语。

items.example: The ending builds reality and activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 reality（真实）与 activity（活动）。

items.example: Urban modernity shaped the novel.
items.exampleCN: 城市现代性塑造了这部小说。

items.example: Modernization preceded modernity in some regions.
items.exampleCN: 在一些地区，现代化先于现代性。

items.meaning: the cultural movement of the new
items.example: Modernism is a movement, not a condition.
items.exampleCN: 现代主义是运动，不是处境。

items.example: The town modernized its port.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇使港口现代化了。

items.example: The modernist preferred the new city.
items.exampleCN: 这位现代主义者更喜欢新城市。

items.example: The station has a modernistic canopy.
items.exampleCN: 车站有一片现代主义风格的顶棚。

definition_zh: 现代化理论；把社会发展解释为从传统到现代若干阶段的理论范式；发展研究中的一套政策框架
definition_en: the body of theory that explains social development as movement from traditional to modern society
core_image: 阶梯教室的黑板上画着从传统到现代的几级台阶，学生把殖民后的港口城市一格一格填进表格
scene: 阶梯教室里，黑板上画着从传统到现代的几级台阶，学生把殖民后的港口城市填进表格，The course applies modernization theory to postcolonial economies.
sceneCN: 这里 modernization theory 指「把发展解释为从传统社会走向现代社会的理论范式」（第 2 个义项：社会学范式）；句意为这门课把现代化理论用于殖民后的经济体。图中可辨识物件：阶梯教室、台阶图、港口城市照片、对照表格。

pos.zh: 现代化理论（发展研究中的理论范式）

现代化理论的阶段划分
